2392def get_compression_type(filepath: str) -> str:
2393    """
2394    The function `get_compression_type` determines the compression type of a file based on its first few
2395    bytes.
2396
2397    :param filepath: The `filepath` parameter is a string that represents the path to the file for which
2398    we want to determine the compression type
2399    :type filepath: str
2400    :return: The function `get_compression_type` returns a string indicating the compression type of the
2401    file specified by the `filepath` parameter. The possible return values are "gzip" if the file is
2402    compressed using gzip, "bgzip" if the file is compressed using bgzip, "unknown" if the compression
2403    type is unknown, and "none" if the file is not compressed.
2404    """
2405
2406    try:
2407        with open(filepath, "rb") as test_f:
2408            # Firsts bits
2409            bit_1 = test_f.read(1)
2410            bit_2 = test_f.read(1)
2411            bit_3 = test_f.read(1)
2412            bit_4 = test_f.read(1)
2413            # If bit is compress
2414            if bit_1 == b"\x1f" and bit_2 == b"\x8b" and bit_3 == b"\x08":
2415                # If bit 4 == x04 is compress 'bgzip' type
2416                if bit_4 == b"\x04":
2417                    return "bgzip"
2418                # else is compress 'gzip' type
2419                else:
2420                    return "gzip"
2421            # If no compress type
2422            else:
2423                return "none"
2424    except:
2425        return "unknown"
2426
2427
2428def get_file_compressed(filename: str = None) -> bool:
2429    """
2430    This function takes a filename as input and returns True if the file is compressed (in bgzip) and False if it
2431    is not
2432
2433    :param filename: the name of the file to be checked
2434    :type filename: str
2435    :return: A boolean value.
2436    """
2437
2438    # Full path
2439    filename = full_path(filename)
2440
2441    compression_type = None
2442    if filename:
2443        # If filename exists, try to detect compression within content (first bits)
2444        if os.path.exists(filename):
2445            compression_type = get_compression_type(filename)
2446        # If filename does not exists, use extension to determine if it is compressed
2447        else:
2448            filename_name, filename_extension = os.path.splitext(filename)
2449            compress_format = filename_extension.replace(".", "")
2450            if compress_format in file_compressed_format:
2451                compression_type = "bgzip"
2452            else:
2453                compression_type = "none"
2454    return compression_type in ["gzip", "bgzip"]
2455
2456
2457def concat_into_infile(
2458    input_files: list,
2459    compressed_file: object,
2460    compression_type: str = "none",
2461    threads: int = 1,
2462    block: int = 10**6,
2463) -> bool:
2464    """
2465    The function `concat_into_infile` concatenates multiple input files into a compressed output file,
2466    with support for different compression types and multi-threading.
2467
2468    :param input_files: A list of input file paths that need to be concatenated into the compressed file
2469    :type input_files: list
2470    :param compressed_file: The `compressed_file` parameter is an object that represents the file where
2471    the concatenated contents of the input files will be written. It is expected to be a file object
2472    that has write capabilities
2473    :type compressed_file: object
2474    :param compression_type: The `compression_type` parameter specifies the type of compression to be
2475    used for the output file. The default value is "none", which means no compression will be applied.
2476    Other possible values include "bgzip" and "gzip", which indicate that the output file should be
2477    compressed using the bgzip and, defaults to none
2478    :type compression_type: str (optional)
2479    :param threads: The "threads" parameter specifies the number of threads to use for compression or
2480    decompression. It determines how many parallel processes can be executed simultaneously, which can
2481    help improve performance when dealing with large files or multiple files, defaults to 1
2482    :type threads: int (optional)
2483    :param block: The `block` parameter is used to specify the size of the block when reading the input
2484    files. It is set to `10 ** 6`, which means 1 million bytes. This parameter determines how much data
2485    is read from the input files at a time
2486    :type block: int
2487    :return: a boolean value, specifically `True`.
2488    """
2489
2490    # Output file compressions type
2491    if compression_type in ["none"]:
2492        open_type = "t"
2493    else:
2494        open_type = "b"
2495
2496    # Open input files
2497    for input_file in input_files:
2498
2499        # Full path
2500        input_file = full_path(input_file)
2501
2502        # Input file compression type
2503        input_compression_type = get_compression_type(input_file)
2504        if input_compression_type in ["bgzip"]:
2505            with open(input_file, "rb") as raw:
2506                with bgzip.BGZipReader(
2507                    raw, num_threads=threads, raw_read_chunk_size=block
2508                ) as infile:
2509                    if open_type in ["t"]:
2510                        compressed_file.write(str(infile.read(), "utf-8"))
2511                    else:
2512                        shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2513        elif input_compression_type in ["gzip"]:
2514            # See https://pypi.org/project/mgzip/
2515            with mgzip.open(input_file, "r" + open_type, thread=threads) as infile:
2516                shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2517        elif input_compression_type in ["none"]:
2518            with open(input_file, "r" + open_type) as infile:
2519                shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2520        else:
2521            raise ValueError(f"Input file compression type unknown: {input_file}")
2522
2523    return True
2524
2525
2526def concat_and_compress_files(
2527    input_files: list,
2528    output_file: str,
2529    compression_type: str = "bgzip",
2530    threads: int = 1,
2531    memory: int = 1,
2532    block: int = 10**6,
2533    compression_level: int = 6,
2534    sort: bool = False,
2535    index: bool = False,
2536) -> bool:
2537    """
2538    The function `concat_and_compress_files` takes a list of input files, an output file name, and
2539    optional parameters for compression type, number of threads, block size, compression level, sorting,
2540    and indexing, and concatenates and compresses the input files into the output file.
2541
2542    :param input_files: A list of input file paths that need to be concatenated and compressed
2543    :type input_files: list
2544    :param output_file: The `output_file` parameter is a string that specifies the path and name of the
2545    output file that will be created after concatenating and compressing the input files
2546    :type output_file: str
2547    :param compression_type: The `compression_type` parameter specifies the type of compression to be
2548    applied to the output file. It can take one of three values: "bgzip", "gzip", or "none", defaults to
2549    bgzip
2550    :type compression_type: str (optional)
2551    :param threads: The `threads` parameter specifies the number of threads to use for compression and
2552    decompression. It determines the level of parallelism in the compression process, allowing for
2553    faster execution when multiple threads are used, defaults to 1
2554    :type threads: int (optional)
2555    :param memory: The `memory` parameter specifies the amount of max memory (in Gb) to use for sorting.
2556    defaults to 1
2557    :type memory: int (optional)
2558    :param block: The `block` parameter specifies the size of the block used for reading and writing
2559    data during compression. It is set to a default value of 10^6 (1 million) bytes
2560    :type block: int
2561    :param compression_level: The `compression_level` parameter determines the level of compression to
2562    be used when compressing the output file. It is an integer value ranging from 0 to 9, where 0
2563    indicates no compression and 9 indicates maximum compression. The higher the compression level, the
2564    smaller the resulting compressed file size, defaults to 6
2565    :type compression_level: int (optional)
2566    :param sort: The `sort` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether the output file should
2567    be sorted or not. If `sort` is set to `True`, the output file will be sorted using
2568    `pysam.bcftools.sort` before renaming it. If `sort` is set to `False, defaults to False
2569    :type sort: bool (optional)
2570    :param index: The `index` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether or not to index the
2571    output file after concatenation and compression. If `index` is set to `True`, the output file will
2572    be indexed using the `pysam.tabix_index` function with the preset "vcf". Make sure VCF is sorted.
2573    Defaults to False
2574    :type index: bool (optional)
2575    :return: a boolean value indicating whether the output file exists or not.
2576    """
2577
2578    # Prevent compression type not available
2579    if compression_type not in ["bgzip", "gzip", "none"]:
2580        compression_type = "bgzip"
2581
2582    # Output file compressions type
2583    if compression_type in ["none"]:
2584        open_type = "t"
2585    else:
2586        open_type = "b"
2587
2588    # Full path
2589    output_file = full_path(output_file)
2590
2591    # Tmp file
2592    output_file_tmp = output_file + "." + str(random.randrange(1000000)) + ".tmp"
2593
2594    # Compression type for first input file
2595    compression_type_input0 = get_compression_type(input_files[0])
2596
2597    log.debug(
2598        f"Concatenate and compress files into '{output_file}' with compression type '{compression_type}'..."
2599    )
2600
2601    # Check single file with same compression type to speed up process
2602    if len(input_files) == 1 and compression_type_input0 == compression_type:
2603        log.debug(
2604            f"Single file with same compression type ({compression_type}): Copy {input_files[0]} to {output_file_tmp}"
2605        )
2606        # os.rename(input_files[0], output_file_tmp)
2607        shutil.copyfile(input_files[0], output_file_tmp)
2608        log.debug(f"File copied: {output_file_tmp}")
2609
2610    # Concat and compress files in gzip
2611    elif compression_type in ["gzip"]:
2612        with pgzip.open(
2613            output_file_tmp,
2614            "w" + open_type,
2615            thread=threads,
2616            blocksize=threads * block,
2617            compresslevel=compression_level,
2618        ) as compressed_file:
2619            concat_into_infile(
2620                input_files,
2621                compressed_file,
2622                compression_type=compression_type,
2623                threads=threads,
2624                block=block,
2625            )
2626
2627    # Concat and compress files in bgzip
2628    elif compression_type in ["bgzip"]:
2629        with open(output_file_tmp, "w" + open_type) as compressed_file_raw:
2630            with bgzip.BGZipWriter(
2631                compressed_file_raw, num_threads=threads
2632            ) as compressed_file:
2633                concat_into_infile(
2634                    input_files,
2635                    compressed_file,
2636                    compression_type=compression_type,
2637                    threads=threads,
2638                    block=block,
2639                )
2640
2641    # Concat and compress files in none
2642    elif compression_type in ["none"]:
2643        with open(output_file_tmp, "w" + open_type) as compressed_file:
2644            concat_into_infile(
2645                input_files,
2646                compressed_file,
2647                compression_type=compression_type,
2648                threads=threads,
2649                block=block,
2650            )
2651
2652    log.debug(
2653        f"Concatenate and compress files into '{output_file}' with compression type '{compression_type}' done."
2654    )
2655
2656    # Output file
2657    if sort:
2658        # Sort with pysam
2659        log.debug(f"Sorting output file...")
2660        try:
2661            pysam.bcftools.sort(
2662                f"-Oz{compression_level}",
2663                "-o",
2664                output_file,
2665                "-T",
2666                output_file_tmp,
2667                output_file_tmp,
2668                "-m",
2669                f"{memory}G",
2670                threads=threads,
2671                catch_stdout=False,
2672            )
2673            # Remove tmp file
2674            os.remove(output_file_tmp)
2675        except:
2676            log.warning(
2677                f"Output file sorting (without tabix) failed: {output_file_tmp}"
2678            )
2679            # Sort with pysam with index before
2680            try:
2681                pysam.tabix_index(output_file_tmp, preset="vcf", force=True)
2682                pysam.bcftools.sort(
2683                    f"-Oz{compression_level}",
2684                    "-o",
2685                    output_file,
2686                    "-T",
2687                    output_file_tmp,
2688                    output_file_tmp,
2689                    "-m",
2690                    f"{memory}G",
2691                    threads=threads,
2692                    catch_stdout=False,
2693                )
2694                # Remove tmp file
2695                os.remove(output_file_tmp)
2696            except:
2697                raise ValueError(
2698                    f"Output file sorting (with tabix) failed: {output_file_tmp}"
2699                )
2700
2701        log.debug(f"Sorting output file done.")
2702
2703    else:
2704        # Rename tmp file
2705        os.rename(output_file_tmp, output_file)
2706
2707    # Index file
2708    if index:
2709        # Index file with tabix
2710        log.debug(f"Indexing output file...")
2711        try:
2712            pysam.tabix_index(output_file, preset="vcf", force=True)
2713        except:
2714            raise ValueError(f"Output file indexing failed: {output_file}")
2715        log.debug(f"Indexing output file done.")
2716
2717    # Return output file
2718    return os.path.exists(output_file)
2719

2721def get_plateform_name_from_duckdb(conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection) -> str:
2722    """
2723    The function `get_plateform_name_from_duckdb` returns the platform information from a DuckDB connection.
2724
2725    :param conn: The `conn` parameter is an instance of the `DuckDBPyConnection` class from the `duckdb`
2726    module. It represents a connection to a DuckDB database
2727    :type conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection
2728    :return: the platform information from the DuckDB connection.
2729    """
2730
2731    return conn.query(f"PRAGMA platform").df()["platform"][0]
2732
2733
2734def get_duckdb_extension_file(
2735    extension_name: str, conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, download: bool = True
2736) -> str:
2737    """
2738    This function returns the file path of a DuckDB extension based on the extension name and platform.
2739
2740    :param extension_name: The name of the DuckDB extension file that is being requested
2741    :type extension_name: str
2742    :return: a string that represents the file path of a DuckDB extension file. The file path is
2743    constructed using the constant `DUCKDB_EXTENSION`, the platform name obtained from the
2744    `get_plateform_name_from_duckdb()` function, and the extension name passed as an argument to the function.
2745    """
2746
2747    # Init
2748    release_version_number = duckdb.__version__
2749    platform_name = get_plateform_name_from_duckdb(conn)
2750
2751    # File
2752    extension_file_path = (
2753        f"v{release_version_number}/{platform_name}/{extension_name}.duckdb_extension"
2754    )
2755    extension_file = f"{DUCKDB_EXTENSION}/{extension_file_path}"
2756    extension_file = full_path(extension_file)
2757    extension_file_gz = f"{extension_file}.gz"
2758    url = f"http://extensions.duckdb.org/{extension_file_path}.gz"
2759
2760    # Download and extract if not exists
2761    if not os.path.exists(extension_file) and download:
2762        # Create folder if not exists
2763        if not os.path.exists(os.path.dirname(extension_file)):
2764            Path(os.path.dirname(extension_file)).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
2765        # Download extension if not exists
2766        if not os.path.exists(extension_file_gz):
2767            try:
2768                download_file(url, extension_file_gz)
2769            except:
2770                log.error(f"Fail download '{url}'")
2771        # Uncompress extention file
2772        if os.path.exists(extension_file_gz):
2773            with mgzip.open(extension_file_gz, "rb", thread=1) as infile:
2774                with open(extension_file, "wb") as compressed_file:
2775                    shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2776
2777    if os.path.exists(extension_file):
2778        return extension_file
2779    else:
2780        return None
2781
2782
2783def load_duckdb_extension(
2784    conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, duckdb_extensions: list
2785) -> bool:
2786    """
2787    This function loads DuckDB extensions into a connection object and returns a boolean indicating
2788    whether all extensions were successfully loaded.
2789
2790    :param conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection object representing a connection to a DuckDB database
2791    :type conn: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection
2792    :param duckdb_extensions: A list of strings representing the names of the DuckDB extensions to be
2793    loaded
2794    :type duckdb_extensions: list
2795    :return: a boolean value indicating whether all the specified DuckDB extensions were successfully
2796    loaded or not.
2797    """
2798
2799    loaded = True
2800
2801    for extension_name in duckdb_extensions:
2802        duckdb_extension_file = get_duckdb_extension_file(
2803            extension_name, conn=conn, download=True
2804        )
2805        try:
2806            if duckdb_extension_file and os.path.exists(duckdb_extension_file):
2807                # Try loading extension by file
2808                conn.query(
2809                    f"INSTALL '{duckdb_extension_file}'; LOAD {extension_name}; "
2810                )
2811            else:
2812                try:
2813                    with time_limit(60):
2814                        # Try loading extension by name
2815                        conn.query(
2816                            f"INSTALL '{extension_name}'; LOAD {extension_name}; "
2817                        )
2818                except:
2819                    loaded = False
2820        except:
2821            try:
2822                with time_limit(60):
2823                    # Try loading extension by name
2824                    conn.query(f"INSTALL '{extension_name}'; LOAD {extension_name}; ")
2825            except:
2826                loaded = False
2827
2828    return loaded
2829
2830
2831class TimeoutException(Exception):
2832    pass
2833
2834
2835def time_limit(seconds):
2836    def signal_handler(signum, frame):
2837        raise TimeoutException("Timed out!")
2838
2839    signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, signal_handler)
2840    signal.alarm(seconds)
2841    try:
2842        yield
2843    finally:
2844        signal.alarm(0)
2845
2846
2847def duckdb_execute(query: str, threads: int = 1) -> bool:
2848    """
2849    The `duckdb_execute` function executes a query using the DuckDB database engine and returns a
2850    boolean indicating whether the query was successful or not.
2851
2852    :param query: The `query` parameter is a string that represents the SQL query you want to execute in
2853    DuckDB. It can be any valid SQL statement, such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, etc
2854    :type query: str
2855    :param threads: The "threads" parameter specifies the number of threads to use for executing the
2856    query. By default, it is set to 1, meaning that the query will be executed using a single thread,
2857    defaults to 1
2858    :type threads: int (optional)
2859    :return: The function `duckdb_execute` returns a boolean value. It returns `True` if the query
2860    execution is successful, and `False` if it is not successful.
2861    """
2862
2863    conn = duckdb.connect(config={"threads": threads})
2864    conn.execute("SET max_expression_depth TO 10000")
2865    if conn.execute(query):
2866        conn.close()
2867        return True
2868    else:
2869        conn.close()
2870        return False
2871

2873def genome_build_switch(assembly: str) -> str:
2874    """
2875    The `genome_build_switch` function takes an assembly name as input and returns a new
2876    assembly name if a different version of the same genome is available, otherwise it returns
2877    None.
2878
2879    :param assembly: The `assembly` parameter is a string that represents the name or identifier
2880    of a genome assembly
2881    :type assembly: str
2882    :return: The function `genome_build_switch` returns a string.
2883    """
2884
2885    import genomepy  # type: ignore
2886
2887    genome_list = genomepy.search(assembly, exact=False)
2888
2889    if genome_list:
2890        for row in genome_list:
2891            tax_id = row[3]
2892            break
2893    else:
2894        log.error(f"Assembly '{assembly}' NOT found")
2895        return None
2896
2897    genome_list = genomepy.search(assembly, exact=False)
2898    for row in genome_list:
2899        new_assembly = row[0].split(".")[0]
2900        new_tax_id = row[3]
2901        if new_assembly != assembly and tax_id == new_tax_id:
2902            return new_assembly
2903
2904    return None

2907# get argument
2908def get_argument(
2909    arguments: dict = {},
2910    arg: str = "",
2911    required: bool = False,
2912    remove_infos: list = ["gooey", "extra"],
2913    add_metavar: bool = False,
2914) -> dict:
2915    """
2916    The `get_argument` function retrieves information about a specific argument from a dictionary, and
2917    can also set its "required" status.
2918
2919    :param arguments: A dictionary containing information about the arguments passed to a function or
2920    method
2921    :type arguments: dict
2922    :param arg: The `arg` parameter is a string that represents the name of the argument that you want
2923    to retrieve information for
2924    :type arg: str
2925    :param required: The `required` parameter is a boolean value that determines whether the argument is
2926    required or not. If set to True, the function will return an empty dictionary if the argument is not
2927    found in the `arguments` dictionary. If set to False (default), the function will still return an
2928    empty dictionary if, defaults to False
2929    :type required: bool (optional)
2930    :param remove_infos: The `remove_infos` parameter is a list that contains the names of specific
2931    information that you want to remove from the argument dictionary. In the code, it is used to remove
2932    specific argument information such as "gooey" from the `arg_infos` dictionary
2933    :type remove_infos: list
2934    :return: a dictionary containing information about a specific argument, specified by the `arg`
2935    parameter. If the argument is found in the `arguments` dictionary, the function returns a dictionary
2936    containing the information about that argument. If the argument is not found, an empty dictionary is
2937    returned. The `required` parameter is used to specify whether the argument is required or not, and
2938    this information is added to
2939    """
2940
2941    if arg in arguments:
2942        arg_infos = arguments.get(arg, {}).copy()
2943        for arg_info in remove_infos:
2944            arg_infos.pop(arg_info, None)
2945        if required != None:
2946            arg_infos["required"] = required
2947        if add_metavar and "metavar" not in arg_infos:
2948            arg_infos["metavar"] = arg.replace("_", " ")
2949        return arg_infos
2950    else:
2951        return {}
2952
2953
2954# get_argument_gooey
2955def get_argument_gooey(arguments: dict = {}, arg: str = ""):
2956    """
2957    The function `get_argument_gooey` takes an argument and returns the corresponding widget and options
2958    for the Gooey library in Python.
2959
2960    :param arg: The `arg` parameter is a string that represents the name of the argument you want to
2961    retrieve information for
2962    :type arg: str
2963    :return: The function `get_argument_gooey` returns two values: `widget` and `options`.
2964    """
2965
2966    # Init
2967    argument = get_argument(arguments=arguments, arg=arg, remove_infos=[])
2968    argument_type = argument.get("type", None)
2969    gooey_argument = argument.get("gooey", {})
2970
2971    # Widget
2972    widget = None
2973    if gooey_argument.get("widget", None):
2974        widget = gooey_argument.get("widget")
2975    else:
2976        if str(argument_type) == "FileType('r')":
2977            widget = "FileChooser"
2978        elif str(argument_type) == "FileType('w')":
2979            widget = "FileSaver"
2980
2981    # options
2982    options = gooey_argument.get("options", {})
2983
2984    # Return
2985    return widget, options

2989def get_argument_to_mk(arg: str, argument: dict = {}, mode: str = "mk") -> str:
2990    """
2991    The function `get_argument_to_mk` generates a formatted string containing information about a
2992    command line argument, which can be output in either Markdown or HTML format.
2993
2994    :param arg: The `arg` parameter is a string that represents the name of the argument. It is used to
2995    generate the header and text for the argument
2996    :type arg: str
2997    :param argument: The `argument` parameter is a dictionary that contains information about the
2998    argument. It has the following keys:
2999    :type argument: dict
3000    :param mode: The `mode` parameter is used to specify the format of the output. It can have two
3001    possible values: "mk" or "html". If "mk" is specified, the output will be formatted using Markdown
3002    syntax. If "html" is specified, the output will be formatted using HTML syntax, defaults to mk
3003    :type mode: str (optional)
3004    :return: a formatted string that provides information about a command line argument. The format of
3005    the string depends on the value of the `mode` parameter. If `mode` is set to "html", the string is
3006    formatted as an HTML `<pre>` block. Otherwise, the string is formatted as a Markdown code block. The
3007    string includes the argument name, metavariable, help text, required
3008    """
3009
3010    from html import escape
3011
3012    text = ""
3013
3014    # Option info
3015    metavar = argument.get("metavar", arg)
3016    help = argument.get("help", None)
3017    required = argument.get("required", None)
3018    choices = argument.get("choices", None)
3019    default = argument.get("default", None)
3020    action = argument.get("action", None)
3021
3022    # header
3023    text_header = f"--{arg}"
3024    if not action:
3025        text_header += f"=<{metavar}>"
3026    if choices:
3027        text_header += f" {choices}"
3028    if default:
3029        text_header += f" (default: {default})"
3030    if required:
3031        text_header += " | required"
3032
3033    # text
3034    if mode == "html":
3035        text += f"<pre>"
3036        text += escape(text_header)
3037        text += "\n"
3038        text += escape(str(help))
3039        text += "\n\n"
3040        text += f"</pre>"
3041    else:
3042        text += "\n<small>\n"
3043        text += "\n> ```\n"
3044        text += f">     {text_header}"
3045        text += "\n> \n> "
3046        text += str(help).strip().replace("\n", "\n> ")
3047        text += "\n> ```\n"
3048        text += "\n</small>\n"
3049        text += "\n"
3050        text += ""
3051
3052    return text
3053

3055def help_generation_from_dict(
3056    element: str,
3057    help_dict: dict,
3058    previous: str = "",
3059    output_type: str = "markdown",
3060    level: int = 1,
3061    table: str = "",
3062    generate_table: bool = False,
3063    code_type: str = "",
3064    auto_default: bool = True,
3065    previous_sections: bool = False,
3066):
3067    """
3068    The `help_generation_from_dict` function generates help documentation from a dictionary input,
3069    supporting markdown and HTML output formats with specific sections like "__help", "__format",
3070    "__default", "__examples", "__code", and "__examples_code".
3071
3072    :param element: The `element` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is a string that
3073    represents the current element or key in the dictionary for which help documentation is being
3074    generated. It is the specific key or element within the dictionary that you want to generate help
3075    documentation for
3076    :type element: str
3077    :param help_dict: The `help_dict` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is a
3078    dictionary that contains the help documentation for various elements or keys. This dictionary
3079    structure allows for organizing and storing information related to each element, such as help text,
3080    formatting details, default values, and examples. The function processes
3081    :type help_dict: dict
3082    :param previous: The `previous` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is used to
3083    keep track of the previous elements in the hierarchy. It is a string that represents the path to the
3084    current element being processed. This parameter helps in maintaining the correct hierarchy level
3085    when generating help documentation for nested elements in a
3086    :type previous: str
3087    :param output_type: The `output_type` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function
3088    specifies the type of output format that you want the generated help documentation to be in. It can
3089    take two possible values: "markdown" or "html". By default, the output type is set to markdown,
3090    defaults to markdown
3091    :type output_type: str (optional)
3092    :param level: The `level` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is used to keep
3093    track of the depth or level of recursion in the generation process. It starts at 1 for the initial
3094    call and increments by 1 for each level of recursion into sub-elements. This parameter helps in
3095    formatting the, defaults to 1
3096    :type level: int (optional)
3097    :param table: The `table` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is used to store the
3098    table of contents for the generated help documentation. It is a string that contains the formatted
3099    table of contents with links to different sections or elements within the documentation. This table
3100    helps users navigate through the documentation easily
3101    :type table: str
3102    :param generate_table: The `generate_table` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is
3103    a boolean flag that determines whether the function should generate a table of contents for the help
3104    documentation. When set to `True`, the function will include a table of contents in the output based
3105    on the hierarchy of elements in the, defaults to False
3106    :type generate_table: bool (optional)
3107    :param code_type: The `code_type` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function specifies
3108    the type of code examples that will be included in the generated help documentation. It defaults to
3109    "json", meaning that the code examples provided in the "__examples_code" section of the dictionary
3110    will be in JSON format
3111    :type code_type: str
3112    :param auto_default: The `auto_default` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict` function is a
3113    boolean flag that determines whether the function should automatically populate certain sections of
3114    the help documentation based on the information available in the dictionary and the element's
3115    arguments. When set to `True`, the function will automatically fill in sections, defaults to True
3116    :type auto_default: bool (optional)
3117    :param previous_sections: The `previous_sections` parameter in the `help_generation_from_dict`
3118    function is a boolean flag that determines whether the function should include previous sections in
3119    the hierarchy when generating help documentation for nested elements. When set to `True`, the
3120    function will maintain the previous sections in the hierarchy path, helping to provide, defaults to
3121    False
3122    :type previous_sections: bool (optional)
3123    :return: The `help_generation_from_dict` function returns the generated help documentation based on
3124    the input `help_dict` dictionary. The output is formatted based on the specified `output_type`
3125    (either "markdown" or "html") and includes sections such as "__help", "__format", "__default", and
3126    "__examples" if they are present in the `help_dict`.
3127    """
3128
3129    from howard.tools.tools import arguments
3130
3131    element_argument_infos = arguments.get(
3132        element, arguments.get(element.replace("_", "-"), {})
3133    )
3134
3135    # Level marker
3136    level_marker = "::"
3137
3138    # Output
3139    output = ""
3140    output_table = ""
3141
3142    # Specific help sections
3143    section_list = [
3144        "__help",
3145        "__type",
3146        "__choices",
3147        "__format",
3148        "__default",
3149        "__default_eval",
3150        "__examples",
3151        "__code",
3152        "__examples_code",
3153    ]
3154
3155    # Previous level
3156    if previous and previous_sections:
3157        prefix = f"{previous}"
3158        previous = f"{prefix}{level_marker}"
3159    else:
3160        prefix = f"{element}"
3161        previous = ""
3162
3163    if "__code_type" in help_dict:
3164        code_type = help_dict.get("__code_type", code_type)
3165
3166    if "__auto" in help_dict:
3167        auto_default = help_dict.get("__auto", True)
3168
3169    if not help_dict:
3170        auto_default = True
3171
3172    if auto_default and level > 1:
3173
3174        # default
3175        if "__help" not in help_dict:
3176            if "help" in element_argument_infos:
3177                help_dict["__help"] = element_argument_infos.get("help", None)  #
3178                # Clean help
3179                help_dict["__help"] = format_arg_help(help_dict["__help"])
3180
3181        # default
3182        if "__default" not in help_dict:
3183            if "default" in element_argument_infos:
3184                help_dict["__default"] = element_argument_infos.get("default", None)
3185
3186        # type
3187        if "__type" not in help_dict:
3188            if "type" in element_argument_infos:
3189                help_dict["__type"] = element_argument_infos.get("type", None).__name__
3190
3191        # format
3192        if "__format" not in help_dict:
3193            if "format" in element_argument_infos:
3194                help_dict["__format"] = element_argument_infos.get("format", None)
3195
3196        # choices
3197        if "__choices" not in help_dict:
3198            if "choices" in element_argument_infos:
3199                help_dict["__choices"] = element_argument_infos.get("choices", None)
3200
3201        # format
3202        if "__format" not in help_dict:
3203            if (
3204                "extra" in element_argument_infos
3205                and "format" in element_argument_infos.get("extra", {})
3206            ):
3207                help_dict["__format"] = element_argument_infos.get("extra", {}).get(
3208                    "format", None
3209                )
3210
3211        # example (code)
3212        if (
3213            "__examples" not in help_dict
3214            and "__examples_code" not in help_dict
3215            and "__code" not in help_dict
3216        ):
3217            if (
3218                "extra" in element_argument_infos
3219                and "examples" in element_argument_infos.get("extra", {})
3220            ):
3221                help_dict["__examples"] = element_argument_infos.get("extra", {}).get(
3222                    "examples", None
3223                )
3224
3225    # If no section "__help" (mandatory)
3226    if "__help" not in help_dict:
3227        return output
3228
3229    # For each help section
3230    for section in section_list:
3231
3232        if section in help_dict:
3233
3234            # If content not empty
3235            if section in help_dict:
3236
3237                # element content
3238                help_dict_content = help_dict.get(section, None)
3239
3240                # Break section
3241                section_break = ""
3242
3243                # Output variables
3244                output_header = ""
3245                output_header_table = ""
3246                output_content = ""
3247
3248                # Markdown
3249                if output_type == "markdown":
3250
3251                    # Level
3252                    level_md = "#" * level
3253
3254                    # line break
3255                    if section in ["__code", "__examples_code", "__examples"]:
3256                        line_break = "\n"
3257                    else:
3258                        line_break = "\n\n"
3259
3260                    # Help content from type
3261                    if isinstance(help_dict_content, str):
3262                        help_md = help_dict_content.replace("\n", line_break)
3263                    # elif isinstance(help_dict_content, list) and section not in ["__choices"]:
3264                    elif (
3265                        isinstance(help_dict_content, list)
3266                        or isinstance(help_dict_content, set)
3267                    ) and section not in ["__choices"]:
3268                        help_md = line_break.join(help_dict_content)
3269                        section_break = "\n"
3270                    else:
3271                        help_md = help_dict_content
3272
3273                    if section in ["__code", "__examples_code", "__examples"]:
3274
3275                        # Format help dict
3276                        # if isinstance(help_md, set):
3277                        #     help_md = list(help_md)
3278                        if isinstance(help_md, str):
3279                            help_md_dict = {}
3280                            example_header = ""
3281                            for example_line in help_md.split("\n"):
3282                                if example_line.startswith("#"):
3283                                    example_header = example_line
3284                                else:
3285
3286                                    if example_header not in help_md_dict:
3287                                        help_md_dict[example_header] = ""
3288                                        example_sep = ""
3289                                    help_md_dict[example_header] += (
3290                                        example_sep + example_line
3291                                    )
3292                                    example_sep = "\n"
3293                        elif isinstance(help_md, dict):
3294                            help_md_dict = help_md
3295                        else:
3296                            help_md_dict = help_md
3297
3298                        # Format examples
3299                        help_md = ""
3300                        for example in help_md_dict:
3301                            example_code = help_md_dict.get(example, "")
3302                            if isinstance(example_code, list):
3303                                example_code = "\n".join(example_code)
3304                            example = re.sub(r"^#*\s*", "", example)
3305                            help_md += f"""\n\n> {example}\n"""
3306                            # Clean example code
3307                            if (
3308                                len(example_code) > 0
3309                                and code_type.upper() == "JSON"
3310                                and example_code.strip()[0] != "{"
3311                            ):
3312                                example_code = example_code.replace("\n", "\n   ")
3313                                example_code = f"""{{\n   {example_code}\n}}"""
3314                            example_code = example_code.replace("\n", "\n> ")
3315                            # Add example code
3316                            help_md += (
3317                                f"""\n> ```{code_type}\n> {example_code}\n> ```"""
3318                            )
3319
3320                    if section in ["__default"]:
3321                        if help_md in [""]:
3322                            help_md = " "
3323                        help_md = f"```{help_md}```"
3324
3325                    if section in ["__default_eval"]:
3326                        help_md = "```" + eval(help_md) + "```"
3327
3328                    if section in ["__type"]:
3329                        help_md = f"```{help_md}```"
3330
3331                    if section in ["__format"]:
3332                        help_md = f"```{help_md}```"
3333
3334                    if section in ["__choices"]:
3335                        help_md = f"```{help_md}```"
3336
3337                    # Output variables
3338                    output_header += f"{level_md} {prefix}\n\n"
3339                    output_header_table += (
3340                        f"#{level_md} Table of contents\n\n{table}\n\n"
3341                    )
3342                    output_content += f"{help_md}\n\n"
3343
3344                # HTML
3345                elif output_type == "html":
3346
3347                    # Level
3348                    level_html = f"H{level}"
3349
3350                    # Help content from type
3351                    if isinstance(help_dict_content, str):
3352                        help_html = help_dict_content.replace("\n", "<br>")
3353                    elif isinstance(help_dict_content, list):
3354                        help_dict_content = map(str, help_dict_content)
3355                        if section in ["__code", "__examples_code", "__examples"]:
3356                            help_html = "\n".join(help_dict_content)
3357                            section_break = ""
3358                        else:
3359                            help_html = "<br>".join(help_dict_content)
3360                            section_break = "<br>"
3361                    elif isinstance(help_dict_content, dict):
3362                        if section in ["__code", "__examples_code", "__examples"]:
3363                            for example_header in help_dict_content:
3364                                help_html = f"{example_header}"
3365                                if isinstance(
3366                                    help_dict_content.get(example_header, []), list
3367                                ):
3368                                    help_html += "\n".join(
3369                                        help_dict_content.get(example_header, [])
3370                                    )
3371                                else:
3372                                    help_html += help_dict_content.get(
3373                                        example_header, ""
3374                                    )
3375                    else:
3376                        help_html = help_dict_content
3377
3378                    if section in ["__code", "__examples_code", "__examples"]:
3379                        help_html = f"<xmp>{help_html}</xmp>"
3380
3381                    # Output variables
3382                    output_header += (
3383                        f"<{level_html} id='{prefix}'>{prefix}</{level_html}>"
3384                    )
3385                    output_header_table += f"""
3386                    <H{level+1}>Table of contents</{level_html}>
3387                    {table}
3388                    <br>
3389                    """
3390                    output_content += f"{help_html}<br>"
3391
3392                # Output section
3393                output_section = re.sub(r"^__", "", section).split("_")[0].capitalize()
3394
3395                # Output construction
3396                if section == "__help":
3397                    output += output_header
3398                    output += output_content
3399                    if table and level == 1:
3400                        output += output_header_table
3401                else:
3402                    output_section = (
3403                        re.sub(r"^__", "", section).split("_")[0].capitalize()
3404                    )
3405                    output += f"{output_section}: {section_break}{output_content}"
3406
3407    # Output table construction
3408    if output_type == "markdown":
3409        output_table += (
3410            "   " * (level - 1)
3411            + f"- [{element}](#{prefix.lower().replace(' ','-').replace(':','')})\n"
3412        )
3413    elif output_type == "html":
3414        output_table += (
3415            "&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;" * (level - 1)
3416            + f"- <a href='#{prefix}'>{element}</a><BR>"
3417        )
3418
3419    # Recusivity to other sub-element
3420    for element in help_dict:
3421
3422        # If element is a sub-element
3423        if element not in section_list and isinstance(
3424            help_dict.get(element, None), dict
3425        ):
3426
3427            # output_tabl
3428            output_table += help_generation_from_dict(
3429                element=element,
3430                help_dict=help_dict.get(element, None),
3431                previous=f"{previous}{element}",
3432                output_type=output_type,
3433                level=level + 1,
3434                table=output_table,
3435                generate_table=True,
3436                code_type=code_type,
3437            )
3438
3439            # Add sub-element output
3440            output += help_generation_from_dict(
3441                element=element,
3442                help_dict=help_dict.get(element, None),
3443                previous=f"{previous}{element}",
3444                output_type=output_type,
3445                level=level + 1,
3446                table=output_table,
3447                code_type=code_type,
3448            )
3449
3450    # Return output
3451    if generate_table:
3452        return output_table
3453    else:
3454        return output

3457def help_generation_from_json(
3458    help_json_file: str,
3459    output_type: str = "markdown",
3460    title="Help",
3461    code_type: str = "",
3462    include_toc: bool = False,
3463):
3464    """
3465    The `help_generation_from_json` function reads a JSON file containing help information, converts it
3466    into a specified output format, and returns the generated help content.
3467
3468    :param help_json_file: The `help_json_file` parameter is a string that should contain the file path
3469    to the JSON file from which help information will be extracted. This JSON file likely contains
3470    structured data that will be used to generate the help content
3471    :type help_json_file: str
3472    :param output_type: The `output_type` parameter in the `help_generation_from_json` function
3473    specifies the format in which the generated help content will be output. By default, it is set to
3474    "markdown", which means the help content will be formatted using Markdown syntax. However, you can
3475    also specify other output formats such, defaults to markdown
3476    :type output_type: str (optional)
3477    :param title: The `title` parameter in the `help_generation_from_json` function is a string that
3478    represents the title of the help documentation that will be generated. It is used to provide a title
3479    for the help content to make it more organized and informative. By default, the title is set to
3480    "Help", defaults to Help (optional)
3481    :param code_type: The `code_type` parameter in the `help_generation_from_json` function is used to
3482    specify the type of code examples that will be included in the generated help content. This
3483    parameter allows you to define the format or language of the code examples to be displayed alongside
3484    the help information extracted from the JSON
3485    :type code_type: str
3486    :param include_toc: The `include_toc` parameter in the `help_generation_from_json` function is a
3487    boolean flag that determines whether a table of contents (TOC) should be included in the generated
3488    help content. If `include_toc` is set to `True`, a table of contents will be generated based,
3489    defaults to False
3490    :type include_toc: bool (optional)
3491    :return: The function `help_generation_from_json` returns the generated help content based on the
3492    information stored in the JSON file provided as input.
3493    """
3494
3495    # Read JSON file
3496    help_dict = {}
3497    with open(help_json_file) as f:
3498        help_dict = yaml.safe_load(f)
3499
3500    # Generate help table of content
3501    if include_toc:
3502        output_table = help_generation_from_dict(
3503            element=title,
3504            help_dict=help_dict,
3505            previous="",
3506            output_type=output_type,
3507            level=1,
3508            generate_table=True,
3509            code_type=code_type,
3510        )
3511    else:
3512        output_table = None
3513
3514    # Generate help
3515    output = help_generation_from_dict(
3516        element=title,
3517        help_dict=help_dict,
3518        previous="",
3519        output_type=output_type,
3520        level=1,
3521        table=output_table,
3522        code_type=code_type,
3523    )
3524
3525    # Return help
3526    return output

3535def get_prog_metadata(
3536    setup: str = None,
3537) -> dict:
3538    """
3539    The `get_prog_metadata` function retrieves metadata information about a program from a
3540    configuration file or from the package metadata, and returns it as a dictionary.
3541    If the metadata is not found, it falls back to default values.
3542
3543    :param setup: The `setup` parameter is a string that represents the path to a configuration file.
3544    This file contains metadata about the program, such as its name, version, description, and long
3545    description content type
3546    :type setup: str
3547    :return: The function `get_prog_metadata` returns a dictionary containing metadata information
3548    about a program. The metadata includes the program name, version, author, and description. If the
3549    metadata is not found in the provided setup file, it falls back to default values or retrieves
3550    """
3551
3552    # Config Parser
3553    # setup = "/tmp/config"
3554    if setup is not None and os.path.isfile(setup):
3555        cf = ConfigParser()
3556        cf.read(setup)
3557        prog_name = cf.get("metadata", "name", fallback="Unknown Program")
3558        prog_version = cf.get("metadata", "version", fallback="0.0.0")
3559        prog_authors = cf.get("metadata", "author", fallback="0.0.0")
3560        prog_description = cf.get(
3561            "metadata", "description", fallback="No description available."
3562        )
3563    else:
3564        # meta
3565        try:
3566            meta = metadata("pyhoward")
3567            prog_name = meta.get("Name")
3568            prog_version = meta.get("Version")
3569            prog_authors = meta.get("author")
3570            prog_description = meta.get("Summary")
3571        # Default
3572        except Exception as e:
3573            print(f"Erreur : {e}")
3574            prog_name = "HOWARD"
3575            prog_version = "0.0.0"
3576            prog_authors = "ALB"
3577            prog_description = "HOWARD - Highly Open Workflow for Annotation & Ranking toward genomic variant Discovery"
3578
3579    # Name clean
3580    prog_name_clean = re.sub(r"^(py)|((?<=\w)py)$", "", prog_name).split("-")[0]
3581
3582    # meta
3583    prog_meta = {}
3584    prog_meta["name"] = prog_name
3585    prog_meta["name_clean"] = prog_name_clean
3586    prog_meta["version"] = prog_version
3587    prog_meta["author"] = prog_authors
3588    prog_meta["description"] = prog_description
3589
3590    # meta return
3591    return prog_meta

3643def help_generation(
3644    arguments_dict: dict = {},
3645    parser=None,
3646    output_type: str = "parser",
3647    setup: str = None,
3648):
3649    """
3650    The `help_generation` function generates a parser object for command-line arguments, as well as
3651    markdown or HTML help documentation for those arguments.
3652
3653    :param arguments_dict: A dictionary containing the arguments for the function. It has three keys:
3654    :type arguments_dict: dict
3655    :param parser: The `parser` parameter is an instance of the `argparse.ArgumentParser` class. It is
3656    used to define the command-line interface and parse the command-line arguments. If no `parser` is
3657    provided, a new instance of `argparse.ArgumentParser` will be created
3658    :param output_type: The `output_type` parameter determines the format of the output. It can be one
3659    of the following values:, defaults to parser
3660    :type output_type: str (optional)
3661    :param setup: The `setup` parameter is a string that represents the path to a configuration file.
3662    This file contains metadata about the program, such as its name, version, description, and long
3663    description content type
3664    :type setup: str
3665    :return: The function `help_generation` returns different outputs based on the value of the
3666    `output_type` parameter.
3667    """
3668
3669    # Arguments
3670    arguments = arguments_dict.get("arguments", {})
3671    commands_arguments = arguments_dict.get("commands_arguments", {})
3672    shared_arguments = arguments_dict.get("shared_arguments", {})
3673
3674    # Parser default
3675    if not parser:
3676        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
3677
3678    # Parser information
3679    parser.prog = get_prog_metadata(setup=setup).get("name_clean", "howard")
3680    parser.description = ""
3681    parser.epilog = (
3682        "\nUsage examples:\n"
3683        + """   howard process --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.annotated.vcf.gz --param=config/param.json \n"""
3684        + """   howard annotation --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.howard.vcf.gz --annotations='tests/databases/annotations/current/hg19/dbnsfp42a.parquet,tests/databases/annotations/current/hg19/gnomad211_genome.parquet' \n"""
3685        + """   howard calculation --input=tests/data/example.full.vcf --output=/tmp/example.calculation.tsv --calculations='vartype' \n"""
3686        + """   howard prioritization --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.prioritized.vcf.gz --prioritization_config=config/prioritization_profiles.json --prioritizations='default,GERMLINE' \n"""
3687        + """   howard query --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --explode_infos --query='SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, "DP", "CLNSIG", sample2, sample3 FROM variants WHERE "DP" >= 50 OR "CLNSIG" NOT NULL ORDER BY "CLNSIG" DESC, "DP" DESC' \n"""
3688        + """   howard stats --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz \n"""
3689        + """   howard convert --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.tsv --explode_infos && cat /tmp/example.tsv \n"""
3690    )
3691    parser.formatter_class = argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter
3692
3693    # Optionals
3694    parser._optionals.title = "Shared arguments"
3695
3696    # Sub parser
3697    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(title="Tools", dest="command")
3698
3699    # Help options
3700    options_md = ""
3701    options_html = ""
3702
3703    # Options for markdown
3704    options_md += f"# HOWARD Help"
3705    options_md += "\n\n"
3706    options_md += f"## Introduction"
3707    options_md += "\n\n"
3708    options_md += "<!--TOC-->"
3709    options_md += "\n\n"
3710    options_md += parser.description.replace("\n", "\n\n")
3711    options_md += re.sub(
3712        r"> $", "", parser.epilog.replace("\n", "\n\n").replace("   ", "> ")
3713    )
3714    options_md += "\n\n"
3715
3716    # Options for HTML
3717    options_html += f"<H1>HOWARD Help</h1>\n"
3718    options_html += "<p>" + parser.description.replace("\n", "<br>") + "</p>"
3719    options_html += parser.epilog.replace("\n", "<br>").replace(
3720        "   ", "&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"
3721    )
3722
3723    # Create commands arguments
3724    for command in commands_arguments:
3725
3726        # Command description
3727        command_description = commands_arguments[command].get("description", "")
3728        command_help = commands_arguments[command].get("help", "")
3729        command_epilog = commands_arguments[command].get("epilog", "")
3730
3731        # Command parser
3732        command_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
3733            command,
3734            description=command_description,
3735            help=command_help,
3736            epilog=command_epilog,
3737            # formatter_class=argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter
3738            # formatter_class=argparse.ArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter
3739            formatter_class=RawTextArgumentDefaultsHelpFormatter,
3740        )
3741
3742        # Markdown
3743        options_md += f"## {command.upper()} tool\n"
3744        options_md += command_description.replace("\n", "\n\n")
3745        options_md += "\n\n"
3746        options_md += re.sub(
3747            r"> $", "", command_epilog.replace("\n", "\n\n").replace("   ", "> ")
3748        )
3749        options_md += "\n\n"
3750
3751        # HTML
3752        options_html += f"<H2>{command.upper()}</H2>\n"
3753        options_html += "<p>" + command_description.replace("\n", "<br>") + "</p>"
3754        options_html += command_epilog.replace("\n", "<br>").replace(
3755            "   ", "&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"
3756        )
3757
3758        # Gooey - add metavar
3759        if output_type == "gooey":
3760            add_metavar = True
3761            command_group_suffix = ""
3762        else:
3763            add_metavar = False
3764            command_group_suffix = " options"
3765
3766        # Main args
3767        command_parser._optionals.title = "Options"
3768        if "main" in commands_arguments[command]["groups"]:
3769            group = "main"
3770            options_md += f"### Main options\n"
3771            options_html += f"<H3>Main options</H3>\n"
3772            for arg in commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group]:
3773                required = commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group][arg]
3774                argument = get_argument(
3775                    arguments=arguments.copy(),
3776                    arg=arg,
3777                    required=required,
3778                    add_metavar=add_metavar,
3779                )
3780                if output_type == "gooey":
3781                    widget, options = get_argument_gooey(arguments=arguments, arg=arg)
3782                    argument["widget"] = widget
3783                    argument["gooey_options"] = options
3784                    if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3785                        argument["help"] = arg
3786                    argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3787                        argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3788                    )
3789                command_parser.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3790                options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3791                options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3792
3793        for group in commands_arguments[command]["groups"]:
3794            if group != "main":
3795                options_md += f"### {group}\n"
3796                options_html += f"<H3>{group}</H3>\n"
3797                command_group = command_parser.add_argument_group(
3798                    f"{group}{command_group_suffix}"
3799                )
3800                for arg in commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group]:
3801                    required = commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group][arg]
3802                    argument = get_argument(
3803                        arguments=arguments.copy(),
3804                        arg=arg,
3805                        required=required,
3806                        add_metavar=add_metavar,
3807                    )
3808                    if output_type == "gooey":
3809                        widget, options = get_argument_gooey(
3810                            arguments=arguments, arg=arg
3811                        )
3812                        argument["widget"] = widget
3813                        argument["gooey_options"] = options
3814                        if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3815                            argument["help"] = arg
3816                        argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3817                            argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3818                        )
3819                    command_group.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3820                    options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3821                    options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3822
3823        # Shared arguments
3824        shared_group = command_parser.add_argument_group("Shared options")
3825        for arg in shared_arguments:
3826            argument = get_argument(
3827                arguments=arguments, arg=arg, required=False, add_metavar=add_metavar
3828            )
3829            if output_type == "gooey":
3830                widget, options = get_argument_gooey(arguments=arguments, arg=arg)
3831                argument["widget"] = widget
3832                argument["gooey_options"] = options
3833                if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3834                    argument["help"] = arg
3835                argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3836                    argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3837                )
3838            shared_group.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3839
3840        options_md += "\n\n"
3841
3842    # Shared arguments for help files
3843    options_md += f"## Shared arguments\n"
3844    options_html += f"<H2>Shared arguments</H2>\n".upper()
3845    for arg in shared_arguments:
3846        required = False
3847        argument = get_argument(arguments=arguments.copy(), arg=arg, required=required)
3848        options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3849        options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3850
3851    # Output
3852    if output_type in ["parser", "gooey"]:
3853        return parser
3854    elif output_type == "markdown":
3855        return options_md
3856    elif output_type == "html":
3857        return options_html
3858    else:
3859        return parser
3860

3862def format_arg_help(help_message: str, default_value: object = None) -> str:
3863    """
3864    The function `format_arg_help` formats a help message for a function argument, including a default
3865    value if provided.
3866
3867    :param help_message: The `help_message` parameter is a string that contains the description or help
3868    message for a function or method argument. It provides information about the purpose or usage of the
3869    argument
3870    :type help_message: str
3871    :param default_value: The `default_value` parameter in the `format_arg_help` function is an optional
3872    parameter that specifies a default value for the argument being described in the help message. If a
3873    default value is provided, it will be included in the formatted help message to indicate the default
3874    value for that argument
3875    :type default_value: object
3876    :return: The function `format_arg_help` returns a formatted help message with a default value
3877    appended at the end if provided.
3878    """
3879
3880    help_return = help_message
3881
3882    random_string = "".join(
3883        random.choices(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits, k=10)
3884    )
3885    help_return = (
3886        re.sub(r"\n\s*-", random_string, help_return)
3887        .replace("\n", " ")
3888        .replace(random_string, "\n-")
3889    )
3890    if default_value:
3891        help_return += "\n(default: " + str(default_value) + ")"
3892
3893    return help_return

3896def bed_sort(input: str, output: str) -> str:
3897    """
3898    The `bed_sort` function reads a tab-separated input file, sorts the data based on columns 0, 1, and
3899    2 in ascending order, and writes the sorted data to a tab-separated output file.
3900
3901    :param input: The `input` parameter is the path to the input file that contains the data to be
3902    sorted. This file should be in a tab-separated format
3903    :type input: str
3904    :param output: The `output` parameter is a string that specifies the path and filename of the output
3905    file where the sorted data will be saved
3906    :type output: str
3907    """
3908
3909    # Read input BED (uncompressed)
3910    # data = pd.read_csv(input, sep="\t", dtype={"chr": "string", "start": "int", "end": "int"}, header=None)
3911    data = pd.read_csv(input, sep="\t", header=None, low_memory=False)
3912
3913    # Sort BED regions
3914    data_sorted = data.sort_values(
3915        [0, 1, 2], axis=0, ascending=True, na_position="first"
3916    )
3917
3918    # Write output BED (uncompressed)
3919    data_sorted.to_csv(output, sep="\t", header=0, index=0)

3922def full_path(path: str) -> str:
3923    """
3924    The function `full_path` takes a path string as input and returns the full expanded path.
3925
3926    :param path: The `full_path` function takes a string `path` as input and returns the full path by
3927    expanding the user's home directory in the path if it is not None
3928    :type path: str
3929    :return: The function `full_path` is returning the expanded version of the input `path` using
3930    `os.path.expanduser(path)`. This function expands the `~` character in the path to the user's home
3931    directory.
3932    """
3933
3934    if isinstance(path, str):
3935        return os.path.abspath(os.path.expandvars(os.path.expanduser(path)))
3936    else:
3937        return path

3971    settings. It is used to collect and store various arguments and their values based on the conditions

3973    :type param: dict

3975    `argparse.Namespace` class, which is typically used to store the command-line arguments parsed by
3976    the `argparse` module in Python. It contains the values of the arguments provided by the user when
3977    the script
3978    :type args: argparse
3979    :param arguments_dict: The `arguments_dict` parameter seems to be a dictionary that likely contains
3980    information about arguments and their default values. This dictionary is used in the function
3981    `set_param` to determine whether a specific argument should be included in the `param` dictionary
3982    based on certain conditions
3983    :type arguments_dict: dict
3984    :param argument: The `argument` parameter in the `set_param` function represents the specific
3985    argument that you want to set in the `param` dictionary. It is the key that will be used to store
3986    the value in the dictionary
3987    :type argument: str
3988    :param section: The `section` parameter in the `set_param` function is used to specify a section
3989    within the `param` dictionary where the argument value should be stored. If a `section` is provided,
3990    the argument value will be stored under that section in the `param` dictionary. If no `section
3991    :type section: str
3992    :return: the updated `param` dictionary after setting the specified argument value based on the
3993    conditions provided in the function.
3994    """
3995
3996    # Argument value
3997    value = vars(args).get(argument, None)
3998
3999    # Sections
4000    if section:
4001        if isinstance(section, str):
4002            sections = section.split(":")
4003        else:
4004            sections = section
4005    else:
4006        sections = []
4007
4008    # Check if to include in param
4009    if argument in args and (
4010        not arguments_dict
4011        or value
4012        not in [get_default_argument(arguments_dict=arguments_dict, argument=argument)]
4013    ):
4014        sections.append(argument)
4015        param = add_value_into_dict(dict_tree=param, sections=sections, value=value)
4016

4020def add_value_into_dict(dict_tree: dict, sections: list = [], value=None):
4021    """
4022    The function `add_value_into_dict` adds a value into a dictionary tree based on the provided
4023    sections.
4024
4025    :param dict_tree: The `dict_tree` parameter is a dictionary representing a tree structure. It serves
4026    as the starting point for adding a value based on the provided sections
4027    :type dict_tree: dict
4028    :param sections: The `sections` parameter in the `add_value_into_dict` function represents a list of
4029    sections corresponding to successive keys in the dictionary. These sections are used to traverse the
4030    dictionary tree and determine the location where the value should be added. Each element in the
4031    `sections` list corresponds to a key in
4032    :type sections: list
4033    :param value: The `value` parameter in the `add_value_into_dict` function represents the value that
4034    you want to add into the dictionary tree at the specified location determined by the `sections`
4035    list. This value can be of any data type (e.g., int, str, list, dict, etc.)
4036    :return: The function `add_value_into_dict` returns the updated dictionary tree after adding the
4037    value based on the given sections.
4038    """
4039
4040    # Pointer to traverse the tree
4041    current_node = dict_tree
4042
4043    # If sections is empty, add the value to the root of the dictionary tree
4044    if not sections:
4045        return current_node
4046
4047    # Traverse the tree based on sections to find the appropriate location for the value
4048    for section in sections[:-1]:
4049        # If the section does not exist yet in the current dictionary, create it
4050        if section not in current_node:
4051            current_node[section] = {}
4052        # Move down the tree following the current section
4053        current_node = current_node[section]
4054
4055    # Add the value to the last section
4056    last_section = sections[-1]
4057    current_node[last_section] = value
4058
4059    return dict_tree
4060

4151    the command-specific arguments that should be processed during argument parsing
4152    :type command: str
4153    :param arguments_list: The `arguments_list` parameter in the `load_args` function is a dictionary
4154    that contains the names of arguments that are expected to be present in the `args` object. This list
4155    is used to specify which arguments should be processed by the function `load_args` during the
4156    argument parsing process
4157    :type arguments_list: dict
4158    :param strict: The `strict` parameter in the `load_args` function is a boolean flag that determines
4159    whether an error should be raised if an argument specified in the `arguments_list` list is not found
4160    in the `args` object. If `strict` is set to `True`, an error will be raised, defaults to False
4161    :type strict: bool (optional)
4162    :return: The function `load_args` is returning a dictionary named `param` after processing the
4163    arguments based on the input parameters and conditions specified in the function.
4164    """
4165
4166    # Variables
4167    arguments_list_to_load = {}
4168    param_section_not_found = get_random(N=16)
4169
4170    # List from command
4171    if command:
4172        command_infos = arguments_dict.get("commands_arguments", {}).get(command, {})
4173        for command_group in command_infos.get("groups", {}):
4174            for command_argument in command_infos.get("groups").get(command_group):
4175                command_group_clean = command_group.replace(" ", "_").lower()
4176                if command_group_clean in ["main"]:
4177                    command_group_clean = None
4178                command_argument = command_argument.replace("-", "_")
4179                arguments_list_to_load[command_argument] = command_group_clean
4180
4181    # Add arguments from arguments
4182    if arguments_list:
4183        for argument in arguments_list:
4184            arguments_list_to_load[argument] = arguments_list.get(argument)
4185
4186    # Load arguments
4187    if arguments_list_to_load:
4188        for argument in arguments_list_to_load:
4189            if argument in args:
4190                section = (
4191                    arguments_dict.get("arguments", {})
4192                    .get(argument, {})
4193                    .get("extra", {})
4194                    .get("param_section", param_section_not_found)
4195                )
4196                if section in [param_section_not_found]:
4197                    section = arguments_list_to_load.get(argument, None)
4198                # section str to list
4199                if isinstance(section, str):
4200                    section = section.split(":")
4201                else:
4202                    section = []
4203                if section_prefix:
4204                    section = section_prefix + section
4205                param = set_param(
4206                    param=param,
4207                    args=args,
4208                    arguments_dict=arguments_dict,
4209                    section=section,
4210                    argument=argument,
4211                )
4212
4213            elif strict:
4214                msg_error = f"Argument '{argument}' not found in list of aguments"
4215                log.error(msg_error)
4216                raise ValueError(msg_error)
4217
4218    return param
4219

4221def get_random(N: int = 10) -> str:
4222    """
4223    The function `get_random` generates a random string of uppercase letters and digits with a default
4224    length of 10.
4225
4226    :param N: The parameter `N` in the `get_random` function represents the length of the random string
4227    that will be generated. By default, if no value is provided for `N`, it will generate a random
4228    string of length 10 consisting of uppercase letters and digits, defaults to 10
4229    :type N: int (optional)
4230    :return: A random string of length N consisting of uppercase letters and digits.
4231    """

4233    return "".join(random.choices(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits, k=N))

4240    This Python function reads a transcripts file into a pandas DataFrame, filtering out comment lines.
4241
4242    :param transcripts_file: The `transcripts_file` parameter is a string that represents the file path
4243    to a file containing transcript information. This function is designed to read the contents of this
4244    file and convert it into a pandas DataFrame. The file is expected to be tab-separated with two
4245    columns: "transcript" and "gene
4246    :type transcripts_file: str
4247    :param column_names: The `column_names` parameter is a list that specifies the column names expected
4248    in the transcripts file. By default, it is set to `["transcript", "gene"]`, indicating that the file
4249    should have two columns named "transcript" and "gene". If the actual column names in the
4250    :type column_names: list
4251    :return: A pandas DataFrame containing transcript and gene information read from the specified file
4252    after filtering out comment lines is being returned.
4253    """
4254
4255    # Full path
4256    transcripts_file = full_path(transcripts_file)
4257
4258    # Transcript dataframe
4259    transcripts_dataframe = pd.DataFrame(columns=column_names)
4260
4261    # If file exists
4262    if transcripts_file and os.path.exists(transcripts_file):
4263
4264        # Data
4265        data = []
4266
4267        # Check column names length by reading all lines
4268        with open(transcripts_file, "r") as f:
4269            for line in f:
4270                # Split line by tab
4271                values = line.strip().split("\t")
4272                data.append(values)
4273
4274        # Convert into DataFrame
4275        transcripts_dataframe_nb_columns = pd.DataFrame(data)
4276
4277        # If dataframe not with the same len than input name columns
4278        if len(transcripts_dataframe_nb_columns.columns) != len(column_names):
4279            column_names_new = []
4280            for i in range(len(transcripts_dataframe_nb_columns.columns)):
4281                if len(column_names) > i:
4282                    column_names_new.append(column_names[i])
4283                else:
4284                    column_names_new.append(f"column_{i+1}")
4285            column_names = column_names_new
4286
4287        # Create dataframe
4288        transcripts_dataframe = pd.read_csv(
4289            transcripts_file,
4290            sep="\t",
4291            header=None,
4292            names=column_names,
4293            index_col=False,
4294        )
4295
4296        # First column
4297        first_column = column_names[0]
4298
4299        # Filter comment on lines
4300        transcripts_dataframe = transcripts_dataframe[
4301            transcripts_dataframe[first_column].str.contains("^[^#]+")
4302        ]

4304    # Return
