def vaf_normalization(row, sample: str) -> str: 
1467def vaf_normalization(row, sample: str) -> str:
1468    """
1469    This function takes in a row of data and a sample name, extracts the genotype information for that
1470    sample, calculates the variant allele frequency (VAF) from the genotype information, and adds the
1471    VAF to the genotype information before returning it.
1472
1473    :param row: The input row of a pandas DataFrame containing information about a genetic variant
1474    :param sample: The parameter "sample" is a string representing the name of the sample for which we
1475    want to calculate the VAF (Variant Allele Frequency). It is used to extract the genotype information
1476    for that particular sample from the input row
1477    :type sample: str
1478    :return: a string that represents the genotype information for a given sample with an added "VAF"
1479    field that represents the variant allele frequency.
1480    """
1481
1482    # format
1483    format_fields = row["FORMAT"].split(":")
1484
1485    # Sample genotype
1486    sample_genotype = row[sample]
1487
1488    # No genotype
1489    if not sample_genotype:
1490        sample_genotype = "./."
1491
1492    # Split samples values values
1493    sample_genotype_infos = sample_genotype.split(":")
1494
1495    # Create Dataframe
1496    sample_genotype_dict = {}
1497    for i in range(len(format_fields)):
1498        if len(sample_genotype_infos) > i:
1499            sample_genotype_dict[format_fields[i]] = sample_genotype_infos[i]
1500        else:
1501            sample_genotype_dict[format_fields[i]] = "."
1502
1503    # Find VAF
1504    # Default VAF
1505    vaf = "."
1506    # VAF from FREQ
1507    if "FREQ" in sample_genotype_dict:
1508        if sample_genotype_dict["FREQ"] != ".":
1509            vaf_freq = sum(
1510                map(float, sample_genotype_dict["FREQ"].replace("%", "").split(","))
1511            )
1512            if vaf_freq:
1513                vaf = round(vaf_freq / 100, 4)
1514    # VAF from DP4
1515    elif "DP4" in sample_genotype_dict:
1516        if sample_genotype_dict["DP4"] != ".":
1517            dp4_split = sample_genotype_dict["DP4"].split(",")
1518            if dp4_split != ["."]:
1519                dp4_dp = sum(map(int, dp4_split))
1520                pd4_alt = sum(map(int, dp4_split[2:]))
1521                vaf = round(pd4_alt / dp4_dp, 6) if dp4_dp else "."
1522    # VAF from AD
1523    elif "AD" in sample_genotype_dict:
1524        if sample_genotype_dict["AD"] != ".":
1525            ad_split = sample_genotype_dict["AD"].split(",")
1526            # if ad_split contains values "."
1527            if "." not in ad_split:
1528                ad_dp = sum(map(int, ad_split))
1529                ad_alt = sum(map(int, ad_split[1:]))
1530                vaf = round(ad_alt / ad_dp, 6) if ad_dp else "."
1531
1532    # add vaf into genotype
1533    sample_genotype_dict["VAF"] = vaf
1534
1535    # Create new genotype info
1536    genotype_with_vaf = ":".join([str(v) for v in sample_genotype_dict.values()])
1537
1538    return genotype_with_vaf

This function takes in a row of data and a sample name, extracts the genotype information for that sample, calculates the variant allele frequency (VAF) from the genotype information, and adds the VAF to the genotype information before returning it.

Parameters
  • row: The input row of a pandas DataFrame containing information about a genetic variant
  • sample: The parameter "sample" is a string representing the name of the sample for which we want to calculate the VAF (Variant Allele Frequency). It is used to extract the genotype information for that particular sample from the input row
Returns

a string that represents the genotype information for a given sample with an added "VAF" field that represents the variant allele frequency.

1541def genotype_stats(df, samples: list = [], info: str = "VAF"):
1542    """
1543    This function computes statistics on a specified information field (e.g. VAF) for a given set of
1544    samples in a pandas dataframe.
1545
1546    :param df: The input dataframe containing variant information
1547    :param samples: The list of sample/pipeline names for which to compute the genotype statistics. If
1548    empty, the function will return an empty dictionary
1549    :type samples: list
1550    :param info: The parameter "info" is a string that represents the type of information being analyzed
1551    in the function. In this case, it is used to compute statistics on the Variant Allele Frequency
1552    (VAF) of genetic variants, defaults to VAF
1553    :type info: str (optional)
1554    :return: a dictionary containing statistics related to a specified information field (default is
1555    "VAF") for a given set of samples in a pandas DataFrame. The statistics include the number of
1556    values, a list of values, minimum value, maximum value, mean, median, and standard deviation. If no
1557    samples are specified, an empty dictionary is returned.
1558    """
1559
1560    # format
1561    format_fields = df["FORMAT"].split(":")
1562
1563    # init
1564    vaf_stats = {
1565        info + "_stats_nb": 0,
1566        info + "_stats_list": None,
1567        info + "_stats_min": None,
1568        info + "_stats_max": None,
1569        info + "_stats_mean": None,
1570        info + "_stats_mediane": None,
1571        info + "_stats_stdev": None,
1572    }
1573
1574    # no sample/pipeline
1575    if not samples:
1576        return vaf_stats
1577
1578    # init
1579    vaf_list = []
1580
1581    # For each sample/pipeline
1582    for sample in samples:
1583
1584        # Split snpeff ann values
1585        sample_infos = df[sample].split(":")
1586
1587        # Create Dataframe
1588        sample_dict = {}
1589        for i in range(len(format_fields)):
1590            if len(sample_infos) > i:
1591                sample_dict[format_fields[i]] = sample_infos[i]
1592
1593        # Check if GT not null
1594        if info in sample_dict:
1595            try:
1596                vaf_float = float(sample_dict[info])
1597            except:
1598                vaf_float = None
1599            if vaf_float:
1600                vaf_list.append(vaf_float)
1601
1602    vaf_stats[info + "_stats_nb"] = len(vaf_list)
1603    if vaf_list:
1604        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_list"] = ":".join([str(x) for x in vaf_list])
1605
1606    # Compute min, max, mean and median only if the list is not empty
1607    if vaf_list:
1608        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_min"] = min(vaf_list)
1609        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_max"] = max(vaf_list)
1610        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_mean"] = statistics.mean(vaf_list)
1611        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_mediane"] = statistics.median(vaf_list)
1612
1613    # Check if there are at least 2 values in the list before computing variance or stdev
1614    if len(vaf_list) >= 2:
1615        vaf_stats[info + "_stats_stdev"] = statistics.stdev(vaf_list)
1616
1617    return vaf_stats

1684    defaults to False

1695    will not use more than 16 threads at a time

1700    :type quiet: bool (optional)
1701    :return: a boolean value indicating whether the file was successfully downloaded and saved to the

1703    """

1706    dest_file_path = full_path(dest_file_path)
1707
1708    # Threads limitation
1709    threads = min(threads, threads_limit)
1710
1711    # Create folder if not exists

1719            # Aria options

1726                aria_redirect_option = ""

1730
1731            # Launch command

1733            try:
1734                output = os.system(
1735                    f"{aria_command} --async-dns={aria_async_dns_option} {aria_redirect_option}"
1736                )
1737                if output:
1738                    assert False
1739            except:
1740                output = os.system(aria_command)
1741
1742            # Test output file
1743            if output or not (
1744                os.path.exists(dest_file_path) and os.stat(dest_file_path).st_size > 0
1745            ):
1746                assert False
1747
1748        else:
1749
1750            assert False
1751
1752    except:
1753
1754        # Request
1755        with requests.get(url, stream=True) as r:
1756            r.raise_for_status()
1757
1758            # Create a temporary file
1759            tmp_file_path = dest_file_path + ".tmp"
1760
1761            # Open the temporary file for writing in binary mode
1762            with open(tmp_file_path, "wb") as f:
1763
1764                # Download the file by chunks
1765                for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=chunk_size):
1766
1767                    # Write the chunk to the temporary file
1768                    f.write(chunk)
1769
1770        # Move the temporary file to the final destination
1771        shutil.move(tmp_file_path, dest_file_path)
1772

2089

2291    memory_str, default_value: int = 1, default_unit: str = "G"
2292) -> int:
2293    """
2294    The `extract_memory_in_go` function converts a memory size string in the format FLOAT[kMG] to an
2295    integer value in Go memory units.
2296
2297    :param memory_str: The `memory_str` parameter should be a string representing a memory value with a
2298    unit suffix in the format FLOAT[kMG]. For example, it could be "1G", "512M", or "2k"
2299    :param default: The `default` parameter in the `extract_memory_in_go` function is used to specify a
2300    default integer value if the conversion of the memory size string fails or if the value cannot be
2301    extracted from the input string. If no valid value can be extracted from the input string, the
2302    function will return the, defaults to 1
2303    :type default: int (optional)
2304    :return: The `extract_memory_in_go` function is returning an integer value representing the memory
2305    size in Go units based on the input memory string provided.
2306    """
2307
2308    # Convert in upper ccase
2309    memory_str = str(memory_str).upper()
2310
2311    # Coefficient
2312    coefficient = {
2313        "K": 1 / (1024 * 1024),
2314        "M": 1 / 1024,
2315        "G": 1,
2316    }
2317
2318    try:
2319        # Extract in float
2320        value = extract_float_from_str(text=memory_str)
2321        if not value:
2322            value = default_value
2323
2324        # Extract unit
2325        unit = re.findall(r"[?([A-Za-z]+", memory_str)
2326        if not unit:
2327            unit = default_unit
2328        else:
2329            unit = unit[0]
2330
2331        # Convert in int Go
2332        if unit in coefficient:
2333            return int(value * coefficient[unit])
2334        else:
2335            raise ValueError(
2336                f"Invalid unit '{unit}'. Use 'k', 'm' ou 'g' i upper or lower case."
2337            )
2338    except ValueError:
2339        raise ValueError(
2340            f"Invalid memory format '{memory_str}'. Use format FLOAT[kMG]."
2341        )

def get_compression_type(filepath: str) -> str: 
2393def get_compression_type(filepath: str) -> str:
2394    """
2395    The function `get_compression_type` determines the compression type of a file based on its first few
2396    bytes.
2397
2398    :param filepath: The `filepath` parameter is a string that represents the path to the file for which
2399    we want to determine the compression type
2400    :type filepath: str
2401    :return: The function `get_compression_type` returns a string indicating the compression type of the
2402    file specified by the `filepath` parameter. The possible return values are "gzip" if the file is
2403    compressed using gzip, "bgzip" if the file is compressed using bgzip, "unknown" if the compression
2404    type is unknown, and "none" if the file is not compressed.
2405    """
2406
2407    try:
2408        with open(filepath, "rb") as test_f:
2409            # Firsts bits
2410            bit_1 = test_f.read(1)
2411            bit_2 = test_f.read(1)
2412            bit_3 = test_f.read(1)
2413            bit_4 = test_f.read(1)
2414            # If bit is compress
2415            if bit_1 == b"\x1f" and bit_2 == b"\x8b" and bit_3 == b"\x08":
2416                # If bit 4 == x04 is compress 'bgzip' type
2417                if bit_4 == b"\x04":
2418                    return "bgzip"
2419                # else is compress 'gzip' type
2420                else:
2421                    return "gzip"
2422            # If no compress type
2423            else:
2424                return "none"
2425    except:
2426        return "unknown"

def concat_into_infile( input_files: list, compressed_file: object, compression_type: str = 'none', threads: int = 1, block: int = 1000000) -> bool: 
2458def concat_into_infile(
2459    input_files: list,
2460    compressed_file: object,
2461    compression_type: str = "none",
2462    threads: int = 1,
2463    block: int = 10**6,
2464) -> bool:
2465    """
2466    The function `concat_into_infile` concatenates multiple input files into a compressed output file,
2467    with support for different compression types and multi-threading.
2468
2469    :param input_files: A list of input file paths that need to be concatenated into the compressed file
2470    :type input_files: list
2471    :param compressed_file: The `compressed_file` parameter is an object that represents the file where
2472    the concatenated contents of the input files will be written. It is expected to be a file object
2473    that has write capabilities
2474    :type compressed_file: object
2475    :param compression_type: The `compression_type` parameter specifies the type of compression to be
2476    used for the output file. The default value is "none", which means no compression will be applied.
2477    Other possible values include "bgzip" and "gzip", which indicate that the output file should be
2478    compressed using the bgzip and, defaults to none
2479    :type compression_type: str (optional)
2480    :param threads: The "threads" parameter specifies the number of threads to use for compression or
2481    decompression. It determines how many parallel processes can be executed simultaneously, which can
2482    help improve performance when dealing with large files or multiple files, defaults to 1
2483    :type threads: int (optional)
2484    :param block: The `block` parameter is used to specify the size of the block when reading the input
2485    files. It is set to `10 ** 6`, which means 1 million bytes. This parameter determines how much data
2486    is read from the input files at a time
2487    :type block: int
2488    :return: a boolean value, specifically `True`.
2489    """
2490
2491    # Output file compressions type
2492    if compression_type in ["none"]:
2493        open_type = "t"
2494    else:
2495        open_type = "b"
2496
2497    # Open input files
2498    for input_file in input_files:
2499
2500        # Full path
2501        input_file = full_path(input_file)
2502
2503        # Input file compression type
2504        input_compression_type = get_compression_type(input_file)
2505        if input_compression_type in ["bgzip"]:
2506            with open(input_file, "rb") as raw:
2507                with bgzip.BGZipReader(
2508                    raw, num_threads=threads, raw_read_chunk_size=block
2509                ) as infile:
2510                    if open_type in ["t"]:
2511                        compressed_file.write(str(infile.read(), "utf-8"))
2512                    else:
2513                        shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2514        elif input_compression_type in ["gzip"]:
2515            # See https://pypi.org/project/mgzip/
2516            with mgzip.open(input_file, "r" + open_type, thread=threads) as infile:
2517                shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2518        elif input_compression_type in ["none"]:
2519            with open(input_file, "r" + open_type) as infile:
2520                shutil.copyfileobj(infile, compressed_file)
2521        else:
2522            raise ValueError(f"Input file compression type unknown: {input_file}")
2523
2524    return True

def concat_and_compress_files( input_files: list, output_file: str, compression_type: str = 'bgzip', threads: int = 1, memory: int = 1, block: int = 1000000, compression_level: int = 6, sort: bool = False, index: bool = False) -> bool: 
2527def concat_and_compress_files(
2528    input_files: list,
2529    output_file: str,
2530    compression_type: str = "bgzip",
2531    threads: int = 1,
2532    memory: int = 1,
2533    block: int = 10**6,
2534    compression_level: int = 6,
2535    sort: bool = False,
2536    index: bool = False,
2537) -> bool:
2538    """
2539    The function `concat_and_compress_files` takes a list of input files, an output file name, and
2540    optional parameters for compression type, number of threads, block size, compression level, sorting,
2541    and indexing, and concatenates and compresses the input files into the output file.
2542
2543    :param input_files: A list of input file paths that need to be concatenated and compressed
2544    :type input_files: list
2545    :param output_file: The `output_file` parameter is a string that specifies the path and name of the
2546    output file that will be created after concatenating and compressing the input files
2547    :type output_file: str
2548    :param compression_type: The `compression_type` parameter specifies the type of compression to be
2549    applied to the output file. It can take one of three values: "bgzip", "gzip", or "none", defaults to
2550    bgzip
2551    :type compression_type: str (optional)
2552    :param threads: The `threads` parameter specifies the number of threads to use for compression and
2553    decompression. It determines the level of parallelism in the compression process, allowing for
2554    faster execution when multiple threads are used, defaults to 1
2555    :type threads: int (optional)
2556    :param memory: The `memory` parameter specifies the amount of max memory (in Gb) to use for sorting.
2557    defaults to 1
2558    :type memory: int (optional)
2559    :param block: The `block` parameter specifies the size of the block used for reading and writing
2560    data during compression. It is set to a default value of 10^6 (1 million) bytes
2561    :type block: int
2562    :param compression_level: The `compression_level` parameter determines the level of compression to
2563    be used when compressing the output file. It is an integer value ranging from 0 to 9, where 0
2564    indicates no compression and 9 indicates maximum compression. The higher the compression level, the
2565    smaller the resulting compressed file size, defaults to 6
2566    :type compression_level: int (optional)
2567    :param sort: The `sort` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether the output file should
2568    be sorted or not. If `sort` is set to `True`, the output file will be sorted using
2569    `pysam.bcftools.sort` before renaming it. If `sort` is set to `False, defaults to False
2570    :type sort: bool (optional)
2571    :param index: The `index` parameter is a boolean flag that determines whether or not to index the
2572    output file after concatenation and compression. If `index` is set to `True`, the output file will
2573    be indexed using the `pysam.tabix_index` function with the preset "vcf". Make sure VCF is sorted.
2574    Defaults to False
2575    :type index: bool (optional)
2576    :return: a boolean value indicating whether the output file exists or not.
2577    """
2578
2579    # Prevent compression type not available
2580    if compression_type not in ["bgzip", "gzip", "none"]:
2581        compression_type = "bgzip"
2582
2583    # Output file compressions type
2584    if compression_type in ["none"]:
2585        open_type = "t"
2586    else:
2587        open_type = "b"
2588
2589    # Full path
2590    output_file = full_path(output_file)
2591
2592    # Tmp file
2593    output_file_tmp = output_file + "." + str(random.randrange(1000000)) + ".tmp"
2594
2595    # Compression type for first input file
2596    compression_type_input0 = get_compression_type(input_files[0])
2597
2598    log.debug(
2599        f"Concatenate and compress files into '{output_file}' with compression type '{compression_type}'..."
2600    )
2601
2602    # Check single file with same compression type to speed up process
2603    if len(input_files) == 1 and compression_type_input0 == compression_type:
2604        log.debug(
2605            f"Single file with same compression type ({compression_type}): Copy {input_files[0]} to {output_file_tmp}"
2606        )
2607        # os.rename(input_files[0], output_file_tmp)
2608        shutil.copyfile(input_files[0], output_file_tmp)
2609        log.debug(f"File copied: {output_file_tmp}")
2610
2611    # Concat and compress files in gzip
2612    elif compression_type in ["gzip"]:
2613        with pgzip.open(
2614            output_file_tmp,
2615            "w" + open_type,
2616            thread=threads,
2617            blocksize=threads * block,
2618            compresslevel=compression_level,
2619        ) as compressed_file:
2620            concat_into_infile(
2621                input_files,
2622                compressed_file,
2623                compression_type=compression_type,
2624                threads=threads,
2625                block=block,
2626            )
2627
2628    # Concat and compress files in bgzip
2629    elif compression_type in ["bgzip"]:
2630        with open(output_file_tmp, "w" + open_type) as compressed_file_raw:
2631            with bgzip.BGZipWriter(
2632                compressed_file_raw, num_threads=threads
2633            ) as compressed_file:
2634                concat_into_infile(
2635                    input_files,
2636                    compressed_file,
2637                    compression_type=compression_type,
2638                    threads=threads,
2639                    block=block,
2640                )
2641
2642    # Concat and compress files in none
2643    elif compression_type in ["none"]:
2644        with open(output_file_tmp, "w" + open_type) as compressed_file:
2645            concat_into_infile(
2646                input_files,
2647                compressed_file,
2648                compression_type=compression_type,
2649                threads=threads,
2650                block=block,
2651            )
2652
2653    log.debug(
2654        f"Concatenate and compress files into '{output_file}' with compression type '{compression_type}' done."
2655    )
2656
2657    # Output file
2658    if sort:
2659        # Sort with pysam
2660        log.debug(f"Sorting output file...")
2661        try:
2662            pysam.bcftools.sort(
2663                f"-Oz{compression_level}",
2664                "-o",
2665                output_file,
2666                "-T",
2667                output_file_tmp,
2668                output_file_tmp,
2669                "-m",
2670                f"{memory}G",
2671                threads=threads,
2672                catch_stdout=False,
2673            )
2674            # Remove tmp file
2675            os.remove(output_file_tmp)
2676        except:
2677            log.warning(
2678                f"Output file sorting (without tabix) failed: {output_file_tmp}"
2679            )
2680            # Sort with pysam with index before
2681            try:
2682                pysam.tabix_index(output_file_tmp, preset="vcf", force=True)
2683                pysam.bcftools.sort(
2684                    f"-Oz{compression_level}",
2685                    "-o",
2686                    output_file,
2687                    "-T",
2688                    output_file_tmp,
2689                    output_file_tmp,
2690                    "-m",
2691                    f"{memory}G",
2692                    threads=threads,
2693                    catch_stdout=False,
2694                )
2695                # Remove tmp file
2696                os.remove(output_file_tmp)
2697            except:
2698                raise ValueError(
2699                    f"Output file sorting (with tabix) failed: {output_file_tmp}"
2700                )
2701
2702        log.debug(f"Sorting output file done.")
2703
2704    else:
2705        # Rename tmp file
2706        os.rename(output_file_tmp, output_file)
2707
2708    # Index file
2709    if index:
2710        # Index file with tabix
2711        log.debug(f"Indexing output file...")
2712        try:
2713            pysam.tabix_index(output_file, preset="vcf", force=True)
2714        except:
2715            raise ValueError(f"Output file indexing failed: {output_file}")
2716        log.debug(f"Indexing output file done.")
2717
2718    # Return output file
2719    return os.path.exists(output_file)

2820                    loaded = False

2822            try:
2823                with time_limit(60):

2826            except:

2848def duckdb_execute(query: str, threads: int = 1) -> bool:
2849    """
2850    The `duckdb_execute` function executes a query using the DuckDB database engine and returns a
2851    boolean indicating whether the query was successful or not.
2852
2853    :param query: The `query` parameter is a string that represents the SQL query you want to execute in
2854    DuckDB. It can be any valid SQL statement, such as SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, etc
2855    :type query: str
2856    :param threads: The "threads" parameter specifies the number of threads to use for executing the
2857    query. By default, it is set to 1, meaning that the query will be executed using a single thread,
2858    defaults to 1
2859    :type threads: int (optional)
2860    :return: The function `duckdb_execute` returns a boolean value. It returns `True` if the query
2861    execution is successful, and `False` if it is not successful.
2862    """
2863
2864    conn = duckdb.connect(config={"threads": threads})
2865    conn.execute("SET max_expression_depth TO 10000")
2866    if conn.execute(query):
2867        conn.close()
2868        return True
2869    else:
2870        conn.close()
2871        return False

3003    syntax. If "html" is specified, the output will be formatted using HTML syntax, defaults to mk
3004    :type mode: str (optional)

3006    the string depends on the value of the `mode` parameter. If `mode` is set to "html", the string is

3008    string includes the argument name, metavariable, help text, required

3011    from html import escape
3012
3013    text = ""

3015    # Option info

3017    help = argument.get("help", None)

3019    choices = argument.get("choices", None)
3020    default = argument.get("default", None)
3021    action = argument.get("action", None)
3022
3023    # header

3025    if not action:
3026        text_header += f"=<{metavar}>"
3027    if choices:

3029    if default:
3030        text_header += f" (default: {default})"
3031    if required:
3032        text_header += " | required"
3033
3034    # text
3035    if mode == "html":
3036        text += f"<pre>"
3037        text += escape(text_header)
3038        text += "\n"
3039        text += escape(str(help))
3040        text += "\n\n"
3041        text += f"</pre>"
3042    else:
3043        text += "\n<small>\n"
3044        text += "\n> ```\n"

def get_prog_metadata(setup: str = None) -> dict: 
3536def get_prog_metadata(
3537    setup: str = None,
3538) -> dict:
3539    """
3540    The `get_prog_metadata` function retrieves metadata information about a program from a
3541    configuration file or from the package metadata, and returns it as a dictionary.
3542    If the metadata is not found, it falls back to default values.
3543
3544    :param setup: The `setup` parameter is a string that represents the path to a configuration file.
3545    This file contains metadata about the program, such as its name, version, description, and long
3546    description content type
3547    :type setup: str
3548    :return: The function `get_prog_metadata` returns a dictionary containing metadata information
3549    about a program. The metadata includes the program name, version, author, and description. If the
3550    metadata is not found in the provided setup file, it falls back to default values or retrieves
3551    """
3552
3553    # Config Parser
3554    # setup = "/tmp/config"
3555    if setup is not None and os.path.isfile(setup):
3556        cf = ConfigParser()
3557        cf.read(setup)
3558        prog_name = cf.get("metadata", "name", fallback="Unknown Program")
3559        prog_version = cf.get("metadata", "version", fallback="0.0.0")
3560        prog_authors = cf.get("metadata", "author", fallback="0.0.0")
3561        prog_description = cf.get(
3562            "metadata", "description", fallback="No description available."
3563        )
3564    else:
3565        # meta
3566        try:
3567            meta = metadata("pyhoward")
3568            prog_name = meta.get("Name")
3569            prog_version = meta.get("Version")
3570            prog_authors = meta.get("author")
3571            prog_description = meta.get("Summary")
3572        # Default
3573        except Exception as e:
3574            print(f"Erreur : {e}")
3575            prog_name = "HOWARD"
3576            prog_version = "0.0.0"
3577            prog_authors = "ALB"
3578            prog_description = "HOWARD - Highly Open Workflow for Annotation & Ranking toward genomic variant Discovery"
3579
3580    # Name clean
3581    prog_name_clean = re.sub(r"^(py)|((?<=\w)py)$", "", prog_name).split("-")[0]
3582
3583    # meta
3584    prog_meta = {}
3585    prog_meta["name"] = prog_name
3586    prog_meta["name_clean"] = prog_name_clean
3587    prog_meta["version"] = prog_version
3588    prog_meta["author"] = prog_authors
3589    prog_meta["description"] = prog_description
3590
3591    # meta return
3592    return prog_meta

def help_generation( arguments_dict: dict = {}, parser=None, output_type: str = 'parser', setup: str = None):

3645    arguments_dict: dict = {},
3646    parser=None,
3647    output_type: str = "parser",

3649):
3650    """
3651    The `help_generation` function generates a parser object for command-line arguments, as well as
3652    markdown or HTML help documentation for those arguments.
3653
3654    :param arguments_dict: A dictionary containing the arguments for the function. It has three keys:

3656    :param parser: The `parser` parameter is an instance of the `argparse.ArgumentParser` class. It is

3658    provided, a new instance of `argparse.ArgumentParser` will be created
3659    :param output_type: The `output_type` parameter determines the format of the output. It can be one
3660    of the following values:, defaults to parser
3661    :type output_type: str (optional)
3662    :param setup: The `setup` parameter is a string that represents the path to a configuration file.
3663    This file contains metadata about the program, such as its name, version, description, and long
3664    description content type

3667    `output_type` parameter.
3668    """
3669
3670    # Arguments
3671    arguments = arguments_dict.get("arguments", {})
3672    commands_arguments = arguments_dict.get("commands_arguments", {})
3673    shared_arguments = arguments_dict.get("shared_arguments", {})
3674
3675    # Parser default
3676    if not parser:
3677        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
3678
3679    # Parser information
3680    parser.prog = get_prog_metadata(setup=setup).get("name_clean", "howard")

3683        "\nUsage examples:\n"
3684        + """   howard process --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.annotated.vcf.gz --param=config/param.json \n"""
3685        + """   howard annotation --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.howard.vcf.gz --annotations='tests/databases/annotations/current/hg19/dbnsfp42a.parquet,tests/databases/annotations/current/hg19/gnomad211_genome.parquet' \n"""
3686        + """   howard calculation --input=tests/data/example.full.vcf --output=/tmp/example.calculation.tsv --calculations='vartype' \n"""
3687        + """   howard prioritization --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.prioritized.vcf.gz --prioritization_config=config/prioritization_profiles.json --prioritizations='default,GERMLINE' \n"""
3688        + """   howard query --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --explode_infos --query='SELECT "#CHROM", POS, REF, ALT, "DP", "CLNSIG", sample2, sample3 FROM variants WHERE "DP" >= 50 OR "CLNSIG" NOT NULL ORDER BY "CLNSIG" DESC, "DP" DESC' \n"""
3689        + """   howard stats --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz \n"""
3690        + """   howard convert --input=tests/data/example.vcf.gz --output=/tmp/example.tsv --explode_infos && cat /tmp/example.tsv \n"""
3691    )
3692    parser.formatter_class = argparse.RawTextHelpFormatter
3693
3694    # Optionals
3695    parser._optionals.title = "Shared arguments"
3696
3697    # Sub parser
3698    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(title="Tools", dest="command")
3699
3700    # Help options
3701    options_md = ""
3702    options_html = ""
3703
3704    # Options for markdown
3705    options_md += f"# HOWARD Help"
3706    options_md += "\n\n"
3707    options_md += f"## Introduction"
3708    options_md += "\n\n"
3709    options_md += "<!--TOC-->"
3710    options_md += "\n\n"
3711    options_md += parser.description.replace("\n", "\n\n")
3712    options_md += re.sub(
3713        r"> $", "", parser.epilog.replace("\n", "\n\n").replace("   ", "> ")
3714    )
3715    options_md += "\n\n"
3716
3717    # Options for HTML
3718    options_html += f"<H1>HOWARD Help</h1>\n"
3719    options_html += "<p>" + parser.description.replace("\n", "<br>") + "</p>"
3720    options_html += parser.epilog.replace("\n", "<br>").replace(
3721        "   ", "&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"
3722    )
3723
3724    # Create commands arguments

3727        # Command description
3728        command_description = commands_arguments[command].get("description", "")
3729        command_help = commands_arguments[command].get("help", "")
3730        command_epilog = commands_arguments[command].get("epilog", "")
3731
3732        # Command parser

3741        )

3745        options_md += command_description.replace("\n", "\n\n")
3746        options_md += "\n\n"
3747        options_md += re.sub(
3748            r"> $", "", command_epilog.replace("\n", "\n\n").replace("   ", "> ")
3749        )
3750        options_md += "\n\n"
3751
3752        # HTML
3753        options_html += f"<H2>{command.upper()}</H2>\n"
3754        options_html += "<p>" + command_description.replace("\n", "<br>") + "</p>"
3755        options_html += command_epilog.replace("\n", "<br>").replace(
3756            "   ", "&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;"
3757        )
3758
3759        # Gooey - add metavar
3760        if output_type == "gooey":
3761            add_metavar = True
3762            command_group_suffix = ""
3763        else:
3764            add_metavar = False
3765            command_group_suffix = " options"
3766
3767        # Main args
3768        command_parser._optionals.title = "Options"
3769        if "main" in commands_arguments[command]["groups"]:
3770            group = "main"
3771            options_md += f"### Main options\n"
3772            options_html += f"<H3>Main options</H3>\n"
3773            for arg in commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group]:
3774                required = commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group][arg]
3775                argument = get_argument(
3776                    arguments=arguments.copy(),
3777                    arg=arg,
3778                    required=required,
3779                    add_metavar=add_metavar,
3780                )
3781                if output_type == "gooey":
3782                    widget, options = get_argument_gooey(arguments=arguments, arg=arg)
3783                    argument["widget"] = widget
3784                    argument["gooey_options"] = options
3785                    if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3786                        argument["help"] = arg
3787                    argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3788                        argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3789                    )
3790                command_parser.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3791                options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3792                options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3793
3794        for group in commands_arguments[command]["groups"]:
3795            if group != "main":
3796                options_md += f"### {group}\n"
3797                options_html += f"<H3>{group}</H3>\n"
3798                command_group = command_parser.add_argument_group(
3799                    f"{group}{command_group_suffix}"
3800                )
3801                for arg in commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group]:
3802                    required = commands_arguments[command]["groups"][group][arg]
3803                    argument = get_argument(
3804                        arguments=arguments.copy(),
3805                        arg=arg,
3806                        required=required,
3807                        add_metavar=add_metavar,
3808                    )
3809                    if output_type == "gooey":
3810                        widget, options = get_argument_gooey(
3811                            arguments=arguments, arg=arg
3812                        )
3813                        argument["widget"] = widget
3814                        argument["gooey_options"] = options
3815                        if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3816                            argument["help"] = arg
3817                        argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3818                            argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3819                        )
3820                    command_group.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3821                    options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3822                    options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3823
3824        # Shared arguments
3825        shared_group = command_parser.add_argument_group("Shared options")
3826        for arg in shared_arguments:
3827            argument = get_argument(
3828                arguments=arguments, arg=arg, required=False, add_metavar=add_metavar
3829            )
3830            if output_type == "gooey":
3831                widget, options = get_argument_gooey(arguments=arguments, arg=arg)
3832                argument["widget"] = widget
3833                argument["gooey_options"] = options
3834                if argument.get("help", "") in ["==SUPPRESS=="]:
3835                    argument["help"] = arg
3836                argument["help"] = format_arg_help(
3837                    argument.get("help", ""), str(argument.get("default", None))
3838                )
3839            shared_group.add_argument(f"--{arg}", **argument)
3840
3841        options_md += "\n\n"
3842
3843    # Shared arguments for help files
3844    options_md += f"## Shared arguments\n"
3845    options_html += f"<H2>Shared arguments</H2>\n".upper()
3846    for arg in shared_arguments:
3847        required = False
3848        argument = get_argument(arguments=arguments.copy(), arg=arg, required=required)
3849        options_md += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument)
3850        options_html += get_argument_to_mk(arg, argument, mode="html")
3851
3852    # Output
3853    if output_type in ["parser", "gooey"]:
3854        return parser
3855    elif output_type == "markdown":
3856        return options_md
3857    elif output_type == "html":
3858        return options_html
3859    else:
3860        return parser

def format_arg_help(help_message: str, default_value: object = None) -> str: 
3863def format_arg_help(help_message: str, default_value: object = None) -> str:
3864    """
3865    The function `format_arg_help` formats a help message for a function argument, including a default
3866    value if provided.
3867
3868    :param help_message: The `help_message` parameter is a string that contains the description or help
3869    message for a function or method argument. It provides information about the purpose or usage of the
3870    argument
3871    :type help_message: str
3872    :param default_value: The `default_value` parameter in the `format_arg_help` function is an optional
3873    parameter that specifies a default value for the argument being described in the help message. If a
3874    default value is provided, it will be included in the formatted help message to indicate the default
3875    value for that argument
3876    :type default_value: object
3877    :return: The function `format_arg_help` returns a formatted help message with a default value
3878    appended at the end if provided.
3879    """
3880
3881    help_return = help_message
3882
3883    random_string = "".join(
3884        random.choices(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits, k=10)
3885    )
3886    help_return = (
3887        re.sub(r"\n\s*-", random_string, help_return)
3888        .replace("\n", " ")
3889        .replace(random_string, "\n-")
3890    )
3891    if default_value:
3892        help_return += "\n(default: " + str(default_value) + ")"
3893
3894    return help_return

3898    """

3900    2 in ascending order, and writes the sorted data to a tab-separated output file.
3901
3902    :param input: The `input` parameter is the path to the input file that contains the data to be

3912    data = pd.read_csv(input, sep="\t", header=None, low_memory=False)

4038    value based on the given sections.

4322    specified `begin` string, it will be skipped and not included in the comparison process. By default,
4323    defaults to ##

4328    using the `strip, defaults to True

4330    :return: The function `identical` is returning a boolean value. It returns `True` if all the lines

4333

4336    for vcf in vcf_list:
4337        vcfs_lines.append([])
4338        with open(vcf, "r") as f:

def check_docker_image_exists(image_with_tag: str) -> bool: 
4352def check_docker_image_exists(image_with_tag: str) -> bool:
4353    """
4354    Checks if a Docker image with a specific tag exists in the local repository.
4355
4356    :param image_with_tag: Image name with tag (e.g., "image:version")
4357    :return: True if the image exists, False otherwise
4358    """
4359    image_name, image_tag = image_with_tag.split(":")
4360    try:
4361        # Run the `docker images` command and capture the output
4362        result = subprocess.run(
4363            ["docker", "images", "--format", "{{json . }}"],
4364            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
4365            stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
4366            text=True,
4367        )
4368        # Check for errors
4369        if result.returncode != 0:
4370            log.warning(f"Error running Docker command: {result.stderr}")
4371            return False
4372
4373        # Search for the image with the specified tag in the command output
4374        for image in result.stdout.split("\n"):
4375            if image:
4376                image_dict = ast.literal_eval(image)
4377                if (
4378                    image_dict.get("Repository") == image_name
4379                    and image_dict.get("Tag") == image_tag
4380                ):
4381                    log.debug(f"Find locally {image_with_tag}")
4382                    return True
4383        return False
4384    except Exception as e:
4385        log.warning(f"Docker image check: {e}")
4386        return False

def docker_automount() -> str: 
4627def docker_automount() -> str:
4628    """
4629     Add needed volume to the tool container, check first if we are already inside one otherwise return empty string
4630    :param containerid: for other linux distribution catch container mount from container ID
4631    :return: string containing volume to add
4632    """
4633    if not os.path.exists("/.dockerenv"):
4634        log.warning("Not inside docker container, block automount option")
4635        return ""
4636
4637    container_id = command(
4638        r"cat /proc/self/cgroup | grep 'docker' | sed 's/^.*\///' | tail -n1"
4639    )
4640    if not container_id:
4641        container_id = command("cat /proc/1/cpuset | cut -d/ -f3")
4642    if not container_id:
4643        raise ValueError("Can't get container ID from within container EXIT")
4644
4645    mounts_new = ""
4646    mounts = json.loads(command(f"docker inspect -f json {container_id}"))[0]["Mounts"]
4647    for volume in mounts:
4648        if "sock" not in volume.get("Source") and "tmp" not in volume.get("Source"):
4649            mounts_new += f" -v {volume.get('Source')}:{volume.get ('Destination')}:{volume.get('Mode')}"
4650    return mounts_new

def contig_sort_key(contig: str) -> tuple: 
4654def contig_sort_key(contig: str) -> tuple:
4655    """
4656    Sort contigs in a VCF file. This function is used as a key function for sorting contigs in a VCF
4657    file. It handles special cases for contig names like 'X', 'Y', 'M', and 'MT'. It also sorts
4658    contigs based on their position as integers. The function returns a tuple with the contig position
4659    and the contig name. Contigs are sorted in ascending order.
4660
4661    :param contig: The contig name to sort.
4662    :type contig: str
4663    :return: A tuple with the contig position and the contig name.
4664    :rtype: tuple
4665    """
4666
4667    # Remove 'chr' from contig
4668    contig_clean = re.sub(r"^chr", "", contig)
4669
4670    # inf
4671    inf = 100000000
4672
4673    # Special cases: X, Y, M/MT
4674    if contig_clean == "X":
4675        return (float(inf) - 3, contig)
4676    elif contig_clean == "Y":
4677        return (float(inf) - 2, contig)
4678    elif contig_clean in ["M", "MT"]:
4679        return (float(inf) - 1, contig)
4680
4681    # Contig as integer
4682    try:
4683        return (int(contig_clean), contig)
4684    except ValueError:
4685        # Contig as on-numeric
4686        return (float(inf), contig_clean)

def sort_contigs(vcf_reader): 
4689def sort_contigs(vcf_reader):
4690    """
4691    Sort contigs in VCF header. This function sorts the contigs in the header of a VCF file based on
4692    their names and positions. It uses the `contig_sort_key` function to sort the contigs. The function
4693    returns a VCF object with sorted contigs. The contigs are sorted in ascending order. The function
4694    modifies the contigs in place.
4695
4696    :param vcf_reader: VCF object from VCF package.
4697    :type vcf_reader: vcf.Reader
4698    :return: VCF object with sorted contigs.
4699    :rtype: vcf.Reader
4700    """
4701
4702    from collections import OrderedDict
4703
4704    # Extract contigs from header
4705    contigs = list(vcf_reader.contigs.keys())
4706
4707    # Sort contigs
4708    sorted_contigs = sorted(contigs, key=contig_sort_key)
4709
4710    # Create new contgis OrderedDict
4711    ordered_contigs = OrderedDict()
4712
4713    # Add contigs
4714    for contig in sorted_contigs:
4715        ordered_contigs[contig] = vcf_reader.contigs[contig]
4716
4717    # Replace contigs
4718    vcf_reader.contigs = ordered_contigs
4719
4720    # Return
4721    return vcf_reader

4900    """
4901    result_describe = conn.execute(query_sql_structure)
4902    description_dict = {row[0]: {"type": row[1]} for row in result_describe.fetchall()}
4903
4904    # Add a select to aggregate list to string if needed
4905    list_columns = []
4906    for column in description_dict:
4907        column_type = description_dict.get(column, {}).get("type", "VARCHAR")
4908        if column_type.endswith("[]"):
4909            list_columns.append(
4910                f""" list_aggregate("{column}", 'string_agg', '{sep}') AS '{column}' """
4911            )
4912        else:
4913            list_columns.append(f""" "{column}" """)
4914
4915    # RE-Query
4916    query_cast = f"""
4917        SELECT {",".join(list_columns)}
4918        FROM ({query})
4919    """
4920
4921    return query_cast

Cast columns of a query to VARCHAR or aggregate arrays to strings.

Parameters
  • query: The original SQL query.
  • conn: The database connection.
  • sep: The separator for list aggregation, defaults to ","
Returns

The modified SQL query with casted columns.

4939    :param assembly: The `assembly` parameter is a string that represents the specific assembly or

4945    If the file is found, it returns the full path to the file.
4946    If the file is not found, it returns None.
4947    :rtype: str or None
4948    """
4949
4950    # Init

4952
4953    # Check if annotation_file exists

4955        annotation_file_found = annotation_file
4956
4957    # Check if full annotation_file exists

4959        annotation_file_found = full_path(annotation_file)
4960
4961    else:
4962

4980            for database in databases_folders
4981        ]

def fast_collect_table_stats( con, table_name, estimate_row_size_mode: str = 'type', samples_size: int = 100000) -> dict: 
5013def fast_collect_table_stats(
5014    con,
5015    table_name,
5016    estimate_row_size_mode: str = "type",
5017    samples_size: int = 100000,
5018) -> dict:
5019    """
5020    Collect fast table statistics from DuckDB.
5021
5022    :param con: DuckDB connection
5023    :type con: duckDB connection
5024    :param table_name: Name of the table to collect stats from
5025    :type table_name: str
5026    :param estimate_row_size_mode: Mode to estimate row size ("type" or "samples")
5027    :type estimate_row_size_mode: str
5028    :param samples_size: Number of samples to use if mode is "samples"
5029    :type samples_size: int
5030
5031    :return: Dictionary with table statistics
5032    :rtype: dict
5033    """
5034
5035    # --- number of rows (DuckDB maintains an internal counter -- very fast)
5036    total_rows = con.execute(f"SELECT count(*) FROM {table_name}").fetchone()[0]
5037
5038    # --- column info
5039    cols = con.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info('{table_name}')").fetchall()
5040    total_cols = len(cols)
5041
5042    # --- estimation of row size by DuckDB type ---
5043    if estimate_row_size_mode == "type":
5044
5045        # Estimated sizes per type (in bytes)
5046        TYPE_SIZES = {
5047            "BOOLEAN": 1,
5048            "TINYINT": 1,
5049            "SMALLINT": 2,
5050            "INTEGER": 4,
5051            "BIGINT": 8,
5052            "REAL": 4,
5053            "DOUBLE": 8,
5054            "TIMESTAMP": 8,
5055            "DATE": 4,
5056            "VARCHAR": 32,  # empirical average estimation
5057            "BLOB": 64,  # estimation
5058        }
5059
5060        # Estimate row size
5061        est_row_size = 0
5062        for (_, name, dtype, *_) in cols:
5063            dtype_u = dtype.upper()
5064            est_row_size += TYPE_SIZES.get(dtype_u, 32)  # fallback = 32 bytes
5065
5066    # --- estimation of row size by sampling ---
5067    elif estimate_row_size_mode == "samples":
5068
5069        # sampling
5070        sample_query = f"""
5071            SELECT *
5072            FROM {table_name}
5073            LIMIT {samples_size}
5074        """
5075        sample_df = con.execute(sample_query).fetchdf()
5076
5077        # Estimate row size from sample
5078        est_row_size = sample_df.memory_usage(deep=True, index=False).sum() / len(
5079            sample_df
5080        )
5081
5082    else:
5083        raise ValueError(
5084            f"Unknown estimate_row_size_mode: {estimate_row_size_mode}. Use 'type' or 'samples'."
5085        )
5086
5087    return {
5088        "total_rows": total_rows,
5089        "total_cols": total_cols,
5090        "avg_row_size": est_row_size,
5091        "table_size_bytes": est_row_size * total_rows,
5092    }

Collect fast table statistics from DuckDB.

Parameters
  • con: DuckDB connection
  • table_name: Name of the table to collect stats from
  • estimate_row_size_mode: Mode to estimate row size ("type" or "samples")
  • samples_size: Number of samples to use if mode is "samples"
Returns

Dictionary with table statistics

def choose_update_strategy_safe( dest_total_rows: int = None, dest_total_cols: int = None, avg_row_size_bytes: int = None, update_cols_count: int = None, update_row_ratio: float = None, ram_available_gb: float = None, chunk_size: int = None, conn=None, dest_table: str = None, sources: list = None, default_join_keys: list = None, samples: int = 10000, memory_safety_factor: float = 0.8, update_penalty: float = 4.0, ctas_penalty: float = 1.5, ctas_threshold: float = 0.2, threads: int = 1): 
5095def choose_update_strategy_safe(
5096    dest_total_rows: int = None,
5097    dest_total_cols: int = None,
5098    avg_row_size_bytes: int = None,
5099    update_cols_count: int = None,
5100    update_row_ratio: float = None,
5101    ram_available_gb: float = None,
5102    chunk_size: int = None,  # not used for now
5103    conn=None,
5104    dest_table: str = None,
5105    sources: list = None,
5106    default_join_keys: list = None,
5107    samples: int = 10000,
5108    memory_safety_factor: float = 0.80,
5109    update_penalty: float = 4.0,
5110    ctas_penalty: float = 1.5,
5111    ctas_threshold: float = 0.20,
5112    threads: int = 1,
5113):
5114    """
5115    Heuristique *robuste OOM-first*.
5116    Retourne ("update" | "ctas", explanation).
5117    """
5118
5119    # Init explanation
5120    explanation = []
5121
5122    # CPU factor
5123    log.debug(f"Adjusting penalties based on {threads} threads.")
5124    cpu_factor = max(1, int(threads) / 1)
5125    update_penalty *= cpu_factor
5126    ctas_penalty *= cpu_factor
5127    explanation.append(f"RAM available: {ram_available_gb}G")
5128    explanation.append(f"CPU factor based on {threads} threads: {cpu_factor:.2f}")
5129    explanation.append(f"update_penalty: {update_penalty}")
5130    explanation.append(f"ctas_penalty: {ctas_penalty}")
5131
5132    # Collect missing table stats
5133    if dest_total_rows is None or dest_total_cols is None or avg_row_size_bytes is None:
5134        fast_stats = fast_collect_table_stats(
5135            con=conn,
5136            table_name=dest_table,
5137            estimate_row_size_mode="samples",
5138            samples_size=samples,
5139        )
5140        dest_total_cols = fast_stats["total_cols"]
5141        dest_total_rows = fast_stats["total_rows"]
5142        avg_row_size_bytes = fast_stats["avg_row_size"]
5143
5144    # --- Fast strategy decision ---
5145    fast_strategy, explanation_fast = choose_update_strategy_fast(
5146        dest_total_rows=dest_total_rows,
5147        dest_total_cols=dest_total_cols,
5148        update_cols_count=update_cols_count,
5149        avg_row_size_bytes=avg_row_size_bytes,
5150        ram_available_gb=ram_available_gb,
5151        update_penalty=update_penalty,
5152        ctas_penalty=ctas_penalty,
5153        safety_factor=memory_safety_factor,
5154    )
5155
5156    # Append explanation
5157    explanation += explanation_fast
5158
5159    # --- Final strategy decision ---
5160    if fast_strategy is not None:
5161        # fast decision possible
5162        explanation.append(f"Fast strategy decided: {fast_strategy.upper()}.")
5163        explanation.append("Estimating update row ratio is NOT required.")
5164        return fast_strategy, explanation
5165    else:
5166        # need to estimate update row ratio
5167        explanation.append("Fast strategy undecided.")
5168        explanation.append("Estimating update row ratio is REQUIRED.")
5169
5170        # --- Estimation update row ratio ---
5171        update_row_ratio = estimate_update_ratio_fast(
5172            conn, dest_table, sources, default_join_keys, samples=samples
5173        )
5174        explanation.append(f"Estimated update ratio: {update_row_ratio:.4f}")
5175
5176        # --- Calculs rows to update ---
5177        rows_to_update = int(dest_total_rows * update_row_ratio)
5178
5179        # RAM available safe
5180        ram_limit_bytes = ram_available_gb * (1024**3) * memory_safety_factor
5181
5182        # --- Estimation memory cost UPDATE ---
5183        update_mem_bytes = rows_to_update * avg_row_size_bytes * update_penalty
5184        log.debug(
5185            f"{update_mem_bytes} = {rows_to_update} * {avg_row_size_bytes} * {update_penalty} > {ram_limit_bytes}"
5186        )
5187
5188        # --- Estimation memory cost CTAS ---
5189        ctas_mem_bytes = dest_total_rows * avg_row_size_bytes * ctas_penalty
5190
5191        explanation += [
5192            f"Cost Update memory: {update_mem_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB",
5193            f"Cost CTAS memory: {ctas_mem_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB",
5194            f"Available safe RAM: {ram_limit_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB",
5195            f"Rows to update: {rows_to_update}",
5196        ]
5197
5198        # --- OOM safe on update strategy (priority) ---
5199        if update_mem_bytes > ram_limit_bytes:
5200            explanation.append(
5201                f"[SAFE] UPDATE memory ({update_mem_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB) "
5202                f"> safe RAM ({ram_limit_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB) -- FORCE CTAS."
5203            )
5204            return "ctas", explanation
5205
5206        # --- OOM safe on ctas strategy ---
5207        if ctas_mem_bytes > ram_limit_bytes:
5208            explanation.append(
5209                f"[SAFE] CTAS memory ({ctas_mem_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB) "
5210                f"> safe RAM ({ram_limit_bytes/1e9:.2f} GB) -- FORCE UPDATE."
5211            )
5212            return "update", explanation
5213
5214        # --- Heuristic "logic" ---
5215        update_col_ratio = update_cols_count / max(dest_total_cols, 1)
5216        if update_col_ratio > ctas_threshold:
5217            explanation.append(
5218                f"Updating {update_col_ratio:.2f} of columns (> {ctas_threshold}) -- CTAS."
5219            )
5220            return "ctas", explanation
5221
5222        # Disabled for now
5223        # if rows_to_update > chunk_size:
5224        #     explanation.append(
5225        #         f"Rows to update {rows_to_update} > chunk_size {chunk_size} -- CTAS."
5226        #     )
5227        #     return "ctas", explanation
5228
5229        explanation.append("Low impact update -- UPDATE chosen.")
5230        return "update", explanation

Heuristique robuste OOM-first. Retourne ("update" | "ctas", explanation).

def choose_update_strategy_fast( dest_total_rows, dest_total_cols, update_cols_count, avg_row_size_bytes, ram_available_gb, update_penalty=4.0, ctas_penalty=1.5, safety_factor=0.75) -> tuple: 
5233def choose_update_strategy_fast(
5234    dest_total_rows,
5235    dest_total_cols,
5236    update_cols_count,
5237    avg_row_size_bytes,
5238    ram_available_gb,
5239    update_penalty=4.0,
5240    ctas_penalty=1.5,
5241    safety_factor=0.75,
5242) -> tuple:
5243    """
5244    Fast heuristic to choose update strategy.
5245    Returns ("update" | "ctas" | None, explanation).
5246
5247    :param dest_total_rows: Total number of rows in the destination table
5248    :type dest_total_rows: int
5249    :param dest_total_cols: Total number of columns in the destination table
5250    :type dest_total_cols: int
5251    :param update_cols_count: Number of columns to be updated
5252    :type update_cols_count: int
5253    :param avg_row_size_bytes: Average size of a row in bytes
5254    :type avg_row_size_bytes: int
5255    :param ram_available_gb: Available RAM in gigabytes
5256    :type ram_available_gb: float
5257    :param update_penalty: Penalty factor for update strategy, defaults to 4.0
5258    :type update_penalty: float
5259    :param ctas_penalty: Penalty factor for CTAS strategy, defaults to 1.5
5260    :type ctas_penalty: float
5261    :param safety_factor: Safety factor for RAM usage, defaults to 0.75
5262    :type safety_factor: float
5263
5264    :return: A tuple containing the chosen strategy ("update", "ctas", or None) and an explanation list.
5265    :rtype: tuple
5266    """
5267
5268    # Init explanation
5269    explanation = []
5270
5271    # Calculate RAM limit in bytes
5272    ram_limit_bytes = ram_available_gb * (1024**3) * safety_factor
5273
5274    # Calculate table size in bytes
5275    table_bytes = dest_total_rows * avg_row_size_bytes
5276
5277    # explanation
5278    explanation.append(f"Table size bytes: {table_bytes}")
5279    explanation.append(f"RAM limit bytes: {ram_limit_bytes}")
5280
5281    # threshold low: UPDATE always safe
5282    n_low = ram_limit_bytes / (avg_row_size_bytes * update_penalty)
5283
5284    # threshold high: CTAS mandatory
5285    n_high = ram_limit_bytes / (avg_row_size_bytes * ctas_penalty)
5286
5287    # Explanation
5288    explanation.append(f"Low memory threshold: {n_low}")
5289    explanation.append(f"High memory threshold: {n_high}")
5290
5291    # If little table -- UPDATE safe
5292    if dest_total_rows < n_low:
5293        # little table -- UPDATE safe -- ratio unnecessary
5294        explanation.append(
5295            f"Table rows {dest_total_rows} < low memory threshold {n_low} -- UPDATE safe."
5296        )
5297        return "update", explanation
5298
5299    # If big table -- CTAS mandatory
5300    if dest_total_rows > n_high:
5301        # table too big -- CTAS mandatory -- ratio unnecessary
5302        explanation.append(
5303            f"Table rows {dest_total_rows} > high memory threshold {n_high} -- CTAS mandatory."
5304        )
5305        return "ctas", explanation
5306
5307    # Medium table -- heuristic on columns
5308    col_ratio = update_cols_count / dest_total_cols
5309    if col_ratio > 0.2:
5310        explanation.append(f"Updating {col_ratio:.2f} of columns (> 0.2) -- CTAS.")
5311        return "ctas", explanation
5312
5313    # Medium table -- heuristic on table size vs RAM
5314    if table_bytes > ram_available_gb * (1024**3) * safety_factor:
5315        explanation.append(
5316            f"Table size bytes {table_bytes} > {safety_factor*100:.0f}% of available RAM -- CTAS."
5317        )
5318        return "ctas", explanation
5319
5320    # otherwise: ambiguous zone -- ratio necessary
5321    return None, explanation

Fast heuristic to choose update strategy. Returns ("update" | "ctas" | None, explanation).

Parameters
  • dest_total_rows: Total number of rows in the destination table
  • dest_total_cols: Total number of columns in the destination table
  • update_cols_count: Number of columns to be updated
  • avg_row_size_bytes: Average size of a row in bytes
  • ram_available_gb: Available RAM in gigabytes
  • update_penalty: Penalty factor for update strategy, defaults to 4.0
  • ctas_penalty: Penalty factor for CTAS strategy, defaults to 1.5
  • safety_factor: Safety factor for RAM usage, defaults to 0.75
Returns

A tuple containing the chosen strategy ("update", "ctas", or None) and an explanation list.

def estimate_update_ratio_fast(con, dest_table, sources, join_keys, samples=1000000): 
5324def estimate_update_ratio_fast(con, dest_table, sources, join_keys, samples=1000000):
5325    join_cols = ", ".join([f'"{k}"' for k in join_keys])
5326    log.debug(f"Estimating update ratio for {dest_table} with join keys: {join_cols}")
5327
5328    # Create temporary table
5329    sample_dest_temporary_name = "dest_sample_" + str(random.randrange(1000000))
5330    con.execute(
5331        f"""
5332        CREATE TEMP TABLE {sample_dest_temporary_name} AS
5333        SELECT {join_cols}
5334        FROM {dest_table}
5335        LIMIT {samples}
5336    """
5337    )
5338
5339    # Sample dest table size
5340    sample_size = con.execute(
5341        f"""
5342        SELECT count(1) as count
5343        FROM {sample_dest_temporary_name} 
5344        LIMIT {samples}
5345    """
5346    ).fetchdf()["count"][0]
5347    log.debug(f"Sampled dest table size: {sample_size}")
5348
5349    if sample_size == 0:
5350        return 0.0
5351
5352    # List to store ratios of each source
5353    ratios = []
5354    for src in sources:
5355        src_table = src["table"]
5356
5357        # Sample source table (same sample size)
5358        src_view_name = "src_sample_" + str(random.randrange(1000000))
5359        log.debug(
5360            f"Created temporary view {src_view_name} for source table {src_table}"
5361        )
5362        con.execute(
5363            f"""
5364            CREATE TEMP VIEW {src_view_name} AS
5365            SELECT {join_cols} 
5366            FROM {src_table} 
5367        """
5368        )
5369
5370        # Count intersection
5371        log.debug(f"Calculate intersection between dest_sample and {src_view_name}")
5372        intersect_count = con.execute(
5373            f"""
5374            SELECT COUNT(1)
5375            FROM {sample_dest_temporary_name} d
5376            JOIN {src_view_name} s USING ({join_cols})
5377        """
5378        ).fetchone()[0]
5379
5380        # Calculate update ratio
5381        ratio = intersect_count / sample_size
5382        log.debug(f"Update ratio = {intersect_count} / {sample_size} = {ratio}")
5383        ratios.append(ratio)
5384
5385        # Cleanup source sample
5386        con.execute(f"DROP VIEW {src_view_name}")
5387
5388    # Cleanup dest sample
5389    con.execute(f"DROP TABLE {sample_dest_temporary_name}")
5390
5391    # Return max ratio
5392    return max(ratios) if ratios else 0.0
def duckdb_has_spilled(temp_dir: str) -> bool: 
5395def duckdb_has_spilled(temp_dir: str) -> bool:
5396    """
5397    Check if DuckDB has spilled to disk in the given temporary directory.
5398    :param temp_dir: The temporary directory used by DuckDB for spill files.
5399    :type temp_dir: Path
5400    :return: True if DuckDB has spilled to disk, False otherwise.
5401    :rtype: bool
5402    """
5403
5404    # Check if temp_dir exists and has any files
5405    if not os.path.exists(temp_dir):
5406        return False
5407
5408    # Check if there are any files in the temp_dir
5409    return any(os.listdir(temp_dir))

Check if DuckDB has spilled to disk in the given temporary directory.

Parameters

Returns

True if DuckDB has spilled to disk, False otherwise.
